articles.title: Tom Brady's NFL Power Rankings: Are The Bears Really The Best Team In The League?
articles.summary: Was the Bears' win over the Seahawks convincing enough to put them at No. 1 over the Bills, 49ers and Broncos in Tom Brady's power rankings?
articles.body: When Tom Brady unveiled his power rankings last week, he teased that the Chicago Bears could jump from No. 6 to No. 1 if they defeated the Seattle Seahawks — and that was before they added All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons. Well, the Bears made it tough for Brady not to be a man of his word this week. They picked up a decisive victory in the defending champs' home stadium, winning 34-17 as Caleb Williams, D'Andre Swift and Simmons all showed out. But other top teams, like the Buffalo Bills and Denver Broncos, also picked up impressive victories in Week 8, making the debate for the No. 1 spot in Brady's power rankings even stronger following the Minnesota Vikings' first loss of the year. So, was Brady a man of his word with his power rankings this week? Here's his full top 10. 10. Pittsburgh SteelersRecord: 6-2Previous ranking: Unranked ↑ Week 8 result: 27-6 win vs. Cleveland Browns Brady's thoughts: I kind of chose a temporary winner from the Cloud of Dust that's the AFC North. The Pittsburgh Steelers, welcome to the top ten. The defense lived in Cleveland's backfield all afternoon, and the offense ran it all over them. Aaron Rodgers and Co. secured their payback for the loss in Cleveland earlier this year. They've won four in a row, hold sole possession of first in the division, and they've got a defense that's been suffocating during the streak. Enjoy the bye, fellas. I think Rodgers has done such a great job playing from the pocket this year. He's always done a great job protecting the football, but I always thought a lot of that was because he could get out of the pocket and turn somewhat would-be sacks or negative plays into big gains because he was outside the pocket. But his transition in is his game — playing from the pocket, still throwing the ball as great as ever, man. He's an ageless wonder. Up next: Bye 9. Kansas City ChiefsRecord: 5-2Previous ranking: 4 ↓ Week 8 result: 28-24 loss at Denver Broncos Brady's thoughts: Two weeks ago, I had the Chiefs at No. 2 when they were unbeaten, and now they've dropped two straight. And this one in Denver kind of stings. K.C. had a lead going into the fourth and didn't score again. Over 100 yards in penalties will do that to you, and I hate pouring salt in the wound, but the knee flinched. The refs made the right call. The good news? Pat Mahomes looked like Pat Mahomes again — three touchdowns, no picks. Clean up the flags, and this offense will be right back in it as the Jets visit Arrowhead. Up next: vs. New York Jets (Sunday) 8. New England PatriotsRecord: 5-3Previous ranking: 9 ↑ Week 8 result: 24-19 win at Miami Dolphins Brady's thoughts: New England went into the half down double digits in Miami — been there before. But they flipped a switch, scoring three straight touchdowns for the win. And Drake Maye was super efficient, throwing for two tuddies, and rushing in another. Mike Vrabel helped steady the ship through some crazy, crazy South Florida weather. I love the humidity these days, but I'm not sure the Pats would agree. Up next, we've got Packers at Patriots on Sunday. I am going to need a new parking pass, though. Hey Vrabes, can you help me out there? I'm always excited to go back to that stadium, to see so many friends that, over the years, have made such a positive difference in my life. There's a big reunion going on for the 2016 team. So many fun things this weekend. I got to make sure I pace myself. We've got Gronk's induction ceremony on Saturday, the game on Sunday and a lot of family and friends. It's gonna be an awesome weekend. Up next: vs. Green Bay Packers (Sunday) 7. Minnesota VikingsRecord: 6-1Previous ranking: 1 ↓ Week 8 result: 19-15 loss at Detroit Lions Brady's thoughts: The victory lap is over, as Minnesota's unbeaten run ends in Detroit. I was there, and the Vikings couldn't slow down the Lions' ground game in the second half and couldn't put a drive together late when they needed a touchdown. But still, they're 6-1 and nobody has allowed fewer points. Now Josh Allen and the Bills are in Minneapolis on Monday night, so not a bad spot to bounce back if they can pull it off. I don't think the Vikings need to bench Kyler Murray. I think Kyler's done a very good job this year. He doesn't turn the ball over much. There was one errant throw on Sunday, but he's done a good job protecting the ball. He can still make plays outside the pocket with his legs when he needs it. And he's a threat to throw the ball downfield. They've got to hit some of those ones to Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison. That would take a lot of pressure off that play-to-play execution. Up next: vs. Buffalo Bills (Monday) 6. Detroit LionsRecord: 5-2Previous ranking: 8 ↑ Week 8 result: 19-15 win vs. Minnesota Vikings Brady's thoughts: I thought about this one for a while, and I had the one-loss Vikings ahead of the Lions at first, but remembered the rule: head-to-head tiebreaker applies in situations where I decide I want to apply it. The Lions ran for over 200 yards, and Jared Goff found Jameson Williams for the go-ahead touchdown late. That connection keeps finding the end zone, and it's turned into one of the most dangerous combos in the league to start the year. Just like that, there are no unbeaten teams left in the NFL, and Detroit's won three in a row. The NFC North is shaping up for some great divisional battles later this year. What's new? Up next: at Miami Dolphins (Sunday) 5. Jacksonville JaguarsRecord: 5-2Previous ranking: 10 ↑ Week 8 result: 42-7 win vs. Indianapolis Colts Brady's thoughts: The runaway watch is officially on in the AFC South, because they blew out the Colts, and this one was over by halftime. Brian Thomas Jr. caught a touchdown a couple of weeks after getting benched in London. And the defense took an interception back almost the length of the field. So, a three-game lead in the division, with a chance to extend it Thursday against a reeling team in Baltimore. Up next: at Baltimore Ravens (Thursday) 4. Denver BroncosRecord: 6-2Previous ranking: 6 ↑ Week 8 result: 28-24 win vs. Kansas City Chiefs Brady's thoughts: There's been a lot of discussion about Bo Nix and his struggles getting the ball down the field this year. And while we were all discussing that, the Broncos just won another game. Down two scores going into the fourth, the defense stepped up with some huge stops. Then, Bo Nix did what he needed to do, helping punch it into the end zone twice. The clutch numbers just keep getting better for this guy. And that's four straight wins. They're unbeaten at home, and they keep finding a way to win late in games. These guys believe in themselves. They believe in each other. And first place in the AFC West belongs to Denver. Up next: at Carolina Panthers (Sunday) 3. San Francisco 49ersRecord: 6-1Previous ranking: 2 ↓ Week 8 result: Idle Brady's thoughts: San Francisco took the week off, and honestly, after that game in Atlanta, they needed it. But getting DeForest Buckner back to the Bay is a solid way to hold a high ranking in a bye week. They're still 6-1, tied with Minnesota for the best record in the NFC, and in control of the NFC West. Up next: vs. Las Vegas Raiders (Sunday) 2. Buffalo BillsRecord: 6-1Previous ranking: 3 ↑ Week 8 result: 36-10 win vs. Baltimore Ravens Brady's thoughts: Buffalo hosted the Ravens, and with Lamar Jackson leaving after one play, we didn't really get to see the game everyone wanted to see. But it created a nice chance for this Buffalo defense to gain a lot of confidence, going against the backup Ravens quarterbacks. Josh Allen is already at 20 total touchdowns on the year. That's insane! And the Bills still have the most points in the NFL. I had them at No. 1 when I first started thinking about this list. They're definitely deserving, but I had another idea. Up next: at Minnesota Vikings (Monday) 1. Chicago BearsRecord: 6-2Previous ranking: 5 ↑ Week 8 result: 34-17 win at Seattle Seahawks Brady's thoughts: Last week, I asked if Chicago could go from No. 5 to No. 1 with a win in Seattle, and I'm a man of my word. The Bears went into Seattle on Monday night and handled their business. D'Andre Swift scored three times, and when Seattle made it a one-score game late, Chicago answered. And, oh yeah, Jeffery Simmons is anchoring the defense from now on. No big deal, right? Look, these are power rankings, not standings, and there's something about the vibe in Chicago that sold me on giving them the top spot. But with great power comes great responsibility, right? Let's see what Caleb Williams can do next. Up next: vs. Tampa Bay Buccaneers (Sunday) FOX SPORTS NEWSLETTERYour teams. Your sports. articles.title: In 2023, Joe Burrow bought a $7.5 million Ohio mansion; years later, his riverfront estate remains a standout purchase
articles.summary: Joe Burrow paid $7.5 million for a three-acre estate in Anderson Township, Ohio, in the summer of 2023.
articles.body: Joe Burrow paid $7.5 million for a three-acre estate in Anderson Township, Ohio, in the summer of 2023. It was the most expensive home sale in Hamilton County that year. The Bengals quarterback bought the 7,300-square-foot house, which looks out over the Ohio River, shortly after signing a five-year, $275 million extension. Reports say he did it quietly, a few months before a wrist injury ended his season in November. Three years later, the purchase still looks smart, and the reasons go well beyond the price.Why Joe Burrow’s $7.5 million Ohio mansion still stands outStart with the timing. Joe Burrow signed the richest deal in NFL history at that point, and a few weeks later he spent about 2.7 percent of it on a house. That is not wild spending for a player earning his money. Most athletes in his position buy fast, buy loud and often buy twice.Burrow did the opposite. He chose a property about 15 minutes from Paycor Stadium, near Coldstream Country Club, in a suburb he could actually live in. No flashy announcement followed. The sale only came to light because public records and a Realtor.com listing gave it away.That restraint is the real story. A $7.5 million home in Cincinnati’s east side buys far more land and privacy than the same money would in Los Angeles or Miami. Burrow got space, quiet and a short commute to work. For a quarterback who gets hit for a living, quiet counts.What you actually get for $7.5 million on the Ohio RiverThe numbers are solid. Reports describe a stucco house of about 7,300 square feet, built in 2016 on former horse farm land. The listing counts 12 rooms. Most accounts say four bedrooms, though a few outlets list five, so the exact layout is worth treating with caution.The setting matters more than the room count. The lot sits on three acres, with open fields, mature trees, a pond and a white wooden fence. The Ohio River bends in the distance. Large windows pull in the light, and the house is described as built with modern, energy-conscious features.Burrow also reportedly planned to add a pool house for extra privacy. That detail says plenty. He was not shopping for a trophy. He was shopping for a place to disappear into on a Tuesday off.Compare that with where he came from. His family home in Athens, Ohio, was bought in 2005 for roughly $240,000. The jump from that house to this one is large, but the thread is the same: stay in Ohio, keep it simple, keep people out.The tax bill that went down and the break-in that rattled the neighborhoodHere is the part most buyers at this level would love. According to the Cincinnati Enquirer, property taxes on the estate fell after county valuations lowered its assessed value. The newspaper also noted that Burrow handled the market well, landing a deal on a home of this size. A record sale price and a smaller tax bill is an unusual pairing.The calm did not last. On a Monday night in December 2024, while Burrow was in Dallas helping Cincinnati to a 27-20 win, someone broke into the house. A person who works for him arrived to find a shattered bedroom window and a home in disarray, then called 911.Police arrested four men in January 2025 after a traffic stop. Authorities said they found items believed to be taken from Burrow’s home, and the group was tied to a string of burglaries at high-value properties across Ohio. Reports described the suspects as Chilean nationals, and the case moved through the local courts afterward.Burrow’s home was not special in that sense. Several NFL stars, including Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce, have dealt with similar break-ins. The lesson for any athlete is blunt: a quiet address helps, but it does not replace real security, especially when your schedule is public and your games are on national television.Why Burrow keeps his money close to CincinnatiLook at the bigger picture and the house makes more sense. Burrow grew up in Ohio, played at Ohio State before transferring to LSU, and has spent his whole pro career with the Bengals. Putting millions into a home near the stadium sends a clear message about where he plans to be.The money side is easy to follow, too. His extension runs through 2028, with earnings climbing each year, and endorsements add several million more. Real estate in a market like Cincinnati holds value well, and a large lot near the river is not something developers can easily replace. If Burrow ever sells, the land alone gives buyers a reason to pay.There is also the human side that numbers miss. Burrow has had a rough few years health-wise, with the wrist injury in 2023 and other setbacks since. A house that lets a player recover in private, away from crowds, is worth more to him than an extra bedroom or a nicer pool.So does the purchase still hold up? On price, privacy and location, yes. The break-in showed the risks that come with fame, but it did not change the basic logic. Burrow bought a place to live rather than a place to be seen, and that choice has aged better than most splashy athlete purchases.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: “A deal could happen at any time": Tyreek Hill's NFL comeback faces major hurdle as teams assess his recovery
articles.summary: Tyreek Hill could still become one of the most fascinating additions to an NFL roster this season.
articles.body: Tyreek Hill could still become one of the most fascinating additions to an NFL roster this season. With the playoff race heating up, teams searching for an offensive spark have a chance to explore a move that would require no trade negotiations. The former Miami Dolphins receiver remains a free agent, leaving the door open for any franchise interested in securing his services. However, his next move depends on more than just his reputation. After a serious knee injury disrupted his 2025 campaign, Hill faces an important challenge before he can return to the field.Tyreek Hill's free agency creates an opportunity for NFL contendersHill's availability presents an unusual opportunity for teams looking to strengthen their passing attacks before the postseason. At 32, the eight-time Pro Bowler still carries a reputation as one of the league's most dangerous deep threats. His speed can change the shape of a defence, even when he is not the primary target.Unlike a player involved in trade discussions, Hill can negotiate directly with any interested franchise. That means teams would not need to surrender valuable draft picks to bring him aboard. For organisations with Super Bowl ambitions, that could make the potential signing particularly attractive.However, his free-agent status does not guarantee an immediate return. Teams must consider whether he can deliver the same explosive performances that made him such a difficult matchup throughout his career.Tyreek Hill's knee recovery remains the biggest obstacle to an NFL returnThe biggest question surrounding Hill is his physical condition. His 2025 season ended in devastating fashion after he suffered a serious left knee injury during Week 4 with Miami. The injury involved a dislocation and multiple torn ligaments, requiring two major surgical procedures.Recovering from such damage takes time, particularly for a receiver whose greatest weapon is his ability to accelerate and create separation. Teams will want more than encouraging rehabilitation reports before making a financial commitment.Hill's agent, Drew Rosenhaus, has continued to signal that a return remains possible. He previously indicated that “a deal could happen at any time”. Still, interested teams are expected to seek complete medical clearance and assess his condition through private workouts.That cautious approach also explains why franchises have explored other receiver options, including Brian Thomas Jr. and Josh Downs, as the November 3 trade deadline approaches.For Hill, the coming weeks could prove decisive. His experience and game-changing ability make him an appealing option, but his recovery must match his ambition. Until teams receive convincing medical assurances, his NFL comeback will remain a possibility rather than a certainty.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.body: The Kansas City Chiefs are reeling from two difficult back to back losses in the new season which seems to have made things difficult for the team in the new season. While all eyes remain on the team for the clash against the New York Jets, the Kansas City Chiefs’ head coach Andy Reid has defended Harrison Butker.Kansas City Chiefs’ head coach Andy Reid makes his stance clear on kicker Harrison Butker after the loss against the Denver BroncosA few hours ago, in an interview, the Kansas City Chiefs’ head coach Andy Reid weighed in on Harrison Butker’s performance at the game against the Denver Broncos as he said, “I could kind of see what he saw on that as far as he ended up going too far right…”The popular head coach said, “But I see why he went right too. We never talk about the protection on that and the overloads on that, but you have a heavy overload on the left side and penetration there.”The Kansas City Chiefs’ head coach Andy Reid continued, “That’s going to alter a kicker. I mean, that’s just what you do as a kicker. It’s no different than what quarterbacks do when they’re throwing the football. So sometimes you have to alter the alignment there. So I get it. It just went a little bit too wide on it. But we’ve got to do a better job of that, of the protection for him.” Reid added: “He kind of had to kick it that way to avoid being blocked.”Andy Reid’s comments sparks a heated debate about Harrison ButkerAndy Reid’s comments about Harrison Butker have now sparked a heated debate as fans have accused him of “protecting” the star kicker.A fan took to X and wrote, “Please ask Andy what has been discussed with Toub regarding Butker’s FG (distance, conditions, situations, etc)? Butker is 33.3% (2 of 6) in 2026 for that range before missing in Denver. Why attempt a 54 yard FG in that situation & conditions with someone only making 33.3%?”Another fan posted, “Even if true (which it’s not) he still fkn missed… stop making bad excuses for the kicker that has the most misses in the league.”A third fan wrote, “I’ve lost so much respect for Andy Reid for keeping him on the roster for this long. Do the right thing Andy. Release him.”However, neither the Kansas City Chiefs’ head coach Andy Reid nor the star player Harrison Butker has responded to the criticisms they are facing.For the unversed, Harrison Butker made a 31 yard field goal, converted a 45 yard field goal to close out the first half, and made all three of his extra point attempts.Later, in the fourth quarter, with the Chiefs trailing, Harrison Butker missed a wide-right 54-yard field goal attempt that would have given Kansas City a 28–27 lead.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Roll The Tape: Meet The Bears' Super Bowl X Factor; The NFL's Most Underrated WR
articles.summary: After diving into the All-22 coaches' film from Week 8, Bucky Brooks examines three new developments to watch.
articles.body: The Detroit Lions offered a blueprint on how to beat the best defense in football. The Chicago Bears added one of the best defenders in football. The Cincinnati Bengals boast the best No. 2 receiver in football. Each week, I dive into the All-22 coaches' film before offering a few insights to watch. Here are three developments that could be long-term storylines involving some of the best teams and players in the NFL. 1.Did The Lions Crack The Code On How To Beat The Vikings' Vaunted Defense? The Lions outsmarted Brian Flores’ impenetrable defense with a throwback formation and running game that left the Vikings defensive wizard desperately searching for answers in a pivotal division matchup this past Sunday. Using a variation of the Power-I formation that was popularized in the 1960s, the Lions ran for 230 yards, with 164 of those yards coming in the second half. The run-heavy formation put a pair of tight ends in front of star running back Jahmyr Gibbs in the backfield, changing the math for a Vikings defense that typically overwhelms opponents with overload pressures in the form of six-plus defenders aggressively attacking gaps at the line of scrimmage. By aligning in an offset formation with the tight ends offset to the right or left of Gibbs, the Lions added two additional gaps to the Vikings’ run fits while creating a moving target for the defenders assigned to those gaps due to the pre-snap motions and shifts of tight ends Sam LaPorta, Brock Wright and Tyler Conklin. Additionally, the unique positioning of Gibbs and Co. behind the offensive guard and tackle created an unbalanced formation with tight ends putting five or six men on one side of the center. While most unbalanced lines are set at the line of scrimmage, forcing the defense to bump over to even up the numbers, the Lions’ backfield formation and pre-snap movement (shifts or motions) kept the Vikings from aligning properly. With the Lions running a "Duo" blocking scheme (man blocking with select double teams at the line of scrimmage) and tight ends inserting into the line at various spots, the Vikings were outnumbered at the point of attack, creating huge running lanes for Gibbs and backup RB Sione Vaki on downhill plays. Although we have watched Rams HC Sean McVay and 49ers HC Kyle Shanahan utilize H-backs, tight ends and wideouts as lead blockers from exotic formations, the Lions’ clever deployment of their tight ends disrupted the Vikings’ blitz scheme by adding extra gaps to defend at the point of attack and varying where those gaps occurred on each play. For a team that had sparingly utilized "13" personnel prior to Week 7, the heavy usage (12 times for 81 rush yards; 83.3% success rate) proved to be the perfect solution to the Vikings’ ultra-aggressive tactics. With the Lions seemingly cracking the code on the Vikings’ aggressive scheme, the rest of the league is scouring the tape to see if they can add a few throwback formations to the call sheet to keep Flores guessing and out of sorts. 2.DT Jeffery Simmons Is A Super Bowl X Factor For Bears When the Bears acquired defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons from the Titans last week for a pair of first-round picks and a fourth-rounder, the three-time All-Pro figured to bolster his new team with his disruptive potential on the interior. At 6-foot-4, 305 pounds, Simmons is an unstoppable force at the point of attack, playing through double teams and combo blocks with poise and persistence. The loquacious defender is also arguably the league’s best trash-talker, with jabbering jaws and a non-stop motor that isn't affected by the scoreboard. Simmons plays each down like the Super Bowl is on the line, and his consistent disruption stems partly from his superior talent and work ethic. He refuses to let double teams slow him down, and his relentlessness shows in his desire to finish at the ball on every play. While most observers focus on his disruptive plays (sacks, tackles for loss and quarterback hits/hurries), it is Simmons’ consistency down in and down out that really transforms a defense. Studying the All-22 coaches’ footage from his Bears debut against the Seahawks in Week 8, Simmons’ energy and effort immediately jumped off the screen. The veteran ran around like a kid in a candy store, sprinting from sideline to sideline to hunt runners down. He also showed the strength and power to hold his position at the point of attack against double teams. When facing one-on-one attention at the line, he repeatedly tossed around his assigned blocker with various power maneuvers, including the bull rush and "club" to quickly disengage and pursue the ball. With Simmons also flashing a unique blend of speed and quickness to complement his superior strength, the Seahawks’ blockers couldn't neutralize him without multiple bodies coming around to shrink his run to the running back or quarterback. The four-time Pro-Bowler refused to stay blocked, and his fanatical effort energized a unit that was looking for a spark at the line of scrimmage. Looking through the tape and reviewing my notes on Chicago DC Dennis Allen’s scheme, it is easy to envision how Simmons’ role will continue to grow with the Bears. The veteran will continue to hold the point with traditional rushes that allow him to plug holes against the run, while taking a straightforward approach to the quarterback. Additionally, Allen will put him on the move in games that let Simmons use his athleticism to blow through cracks created by the choreographed movement at the line of scrimmage. With the Bears likely to add more rushers in five- and six-man pressures, Simmons should walk into sacks against overwhelmed blockers unable to handle his physicality and Allen’s creativity. Chicago's marquee addition cost a pretty penny, but his talent and tools will transform the defense into a top-notch unit that creates the kind of chaos and havoc opposing quarterbacks and playcallers fear. With the move pushing the Super Bowl-starved franchise into title contention, Simmons’ disruption and dominance could add some more hardware to the trophy case in Halas Hall at season’s end. 3.Tee Higgins Is The Best WR2 In The NFL We are only two seasons removed from Ja’Marr Chase claiming the NFL’s WR1 title after becoming the sixth player in the Super Bowl era to win the "Triple Crown" as the single-season leader in receptions (127), receiving yards (1,708) and touchdowns (17). While the three-time All-Pro is still worthy of wearing the crown after another phenomenal season in 2025 that showcased his dominance as a playmaker, the Bengals can now lay claim to boasting the league’s best WR2. Tee Higgins, if you haven't noticed, has fully emerged as an unstoppable force on the perimeter for the 5-2 Bengals. The 6-foot-4, 220-pounder has opened the 2026 season on a heater with 43 catches, 726 receiving yards (second in the NFL) and four touchdowns through seven games. Higgins is averaging 103.7 receiving yards per game and 16.9 yards per catch, reflecting his big-play potential as a vertical threat. Moreover, the 2025 Pro Bowler has dominated his one-on-one matchups, using his size, length and athleticism to overwhelm defenders on jump balls down the boundary or in the red zone. It's worth noting Higgins was a high school basketball standout who had several D1 offers (Louisville, Tennessee, Auburn, Middle Tennessee State, and others) before deciding to play football at Clemson. The seventh-year pro’s hardwood skills repeatedly show up on the grass when he "boxes out" defenders to win contested catches. According to Next Gen Stats, Higgins has been one of the league’s most productive targets on tight-window throws (where the ball arrives with less than a yard of separation), which speaks to Joe Burrow's trust in the extra-long, rangy receiver. Studying the All-22 coaches’ tape, you see why the star quarterback is not afraid to target the veteran with defenders around. Higgins’ length and strength make it hard for defenders to wrestle the ball out of his hands when he hauls in a fade ball down the boundary. Additionally, Higgins excels at "high-pointing" alley-oops, like a back-door lob against a 2-3 zone defense. With Higgins flashing impressive route-running skills as a long strider with surprising agility and stop-and-start quickness, the Bengals have been able to feature their WR2 on more than just classic vertical routes (go routes and skinny posts) downfield. He can run the entire route tree out wide, with comebacks, digs and back-shoulder fades ranking as his best routes in the Bengals’ scheme. Given Higgins’ production opposite Chase, it is fair to wonder how he would fare on his own as a No. 1 option in the passing game. He has shown "take-over-the-game" potential when occupying the WR1 role, with 36 receptions, 542 receiving yards and three touchdowns in six games without Chase. Those numbers are solid and not significantly greater than Higgins’ weekly stat line, which suggests his output is sustainable as a WR1 or WR2 for the Bengals. At a time when coaches and scouts want consistency and dependability from a second wide receiver, it is hard to knock Higgins off the pedestal as the best No. 2 in football.

articles.title: NFL Thursday Night Football preview: Ravens to start rookie Joe Fagnano at QB vs. Jaguars
articles.summary: The Jaguars will be going against the Ravens' third quarterback of the season.
articles.body:
The Baltimore Ravens had hope before kickoff last Sunday. Ahead of their kickoff on Thursday, most of that hope has vanished with two months left in the season.

The Ravens suffered not one but two quarterback injuries on Sunday. Lamar Jackson dislocated his right thumb on his first play back from an ankle injury, then Tyler Huntley injured his toe. Both players are on injured reserve.

Before last Sunday, you would have had to have watched a lot of preseason football to know Joe Fagnano was the Ravens' third-string quarterback. The undrafted rookie is now elevated to QB1 for their game on Thursday night against a very good Jacksonville Jaguars team. There is help on the way next week, as the Ravens reportedly were finalizing a deal for Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett, but Fagnano will get at least one start.

Fagnano started his college career as a walk-on at Maine. He went to UConn after that and had an impressive 28-to-1 touchdown-to-interception ratio for the Huskies. He still went undrafted and signed with the Ravens with no money guaranteed. In his first NFL action last week, he completed 10-of-21 passes for 91 yards. He will benefit from getting starter's reps in practice, even though it's a short week. It's still a very tough assignment.

The Jaguars are 5-2 and lead the NFL with a +85 point differential. They're up to No. 2 in DVOA behind the 49ers and are the only team that ranks in the top-five of offense, defense and special teams in DVOA. Three of their five wins have come by 24 or more points. It looks like they'll run away with the AFC South.

The Ravens are just trying to stay alive in case Jackson can make a return sometime late in the season. They have to wait one more week for Brissett to be the bridge quarterback to that. This week, they're relying on an undrafted rookie to help pull off an improbable win.

It's reasonable to say the Ravens. If they win they'll be 5-4 with Jacoby Brissett coming on board. The season wouldn't technically be over at that point. However, Baltimore's chances of staying afloat over the second half of the season and also having Lamar Jackson return are slim. When you lose a two-time MVP quarterback to injured reserve, there's not much you can do about it. The Jaguars are cruising along at 5-2 and look like a legitimate Super Bowl contender. They might not be the more desperate team, but they're the one with a bright future this season. They need it more just because a loss to a reeling team with an undrafted rookie quarterback would poor cold water on the idea that the Jaguars can win a championship.

If the Ravens can pull off an upset, it will be because the defense plays great and the offense carries its quarterback. That formula puts a lot of pressure on Henry. It won't be easy against a Jaguars team that will likely come in not respecting the Ravens' passing game with a rookie making his first start. The Jaguars also allow the fewest rushing yards and rushing yards per carry in the NFL. That did come with defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton having a good season, and he suffered a season-ending quad injury last week. Henry had a good start to the season, but has had some quiet games lately with the Ravens suffering through bad quarterback play. He has 156 yards on 45 carries (3.5-yard average) over the last three weeks, and Baltimore hasn't scored more than 13 points in any of those games. But they need Henry to have a dominant performance Thursday, and that won't be easy against a good Jaguars defense.

The Jaguars travel to Baltimore to take on the M.A.S.H. unit that is the Ravens' remaining roster on Thursday night. Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley? Both out on IR. Third-stringer Joe Fagnano will start, but is dealing with an ankle injury. Baltimore is reportedly trading for Jacoby Brissett, but he won't be playing this week. To put a little context into the state of both teams, this line was Ravens -4.5 this offseason, it re-opened Ravens +8 on Sunday and got as high as +10. The Jaguars are only 4-3 against the spread this season, but they're coming off a 42-7 rout of an undermanned Colts team. Baltimore has talent on both sides of the ball, but this is a big ask for Fagnano — on a short week and with an injury no less. There are some Jacksonville -9.5s out there in the market. I'd jump on one of those or put Jacksonville in a 7-point tease with the 49ers -9.5 to get both under a field goal. — Ben Fawkes

Check out more of Ben's work at the Yahoo Sports betting hub .

Jacksonville at Baltimore looked like a signature game when the schedule was released, but all bets are off with Lamar Jackson unavailable. Here are three fantasy angles to track as you watch the game.

1. Can Zay Flowers survive? Flowers has shown the ability to produce with backups before — he was just fine with Tyler Huntley last year. But with Jackson and Huntley both unavailable and Jacoby Brissett a week away, the Ravens have to make do with undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano in this spot. Flowers did not have a catch in the loss to Buffalo.

2. What does the Jacksonville pass distribution look like? Although Trevor Lawrence attempted just 14 passes last week, he found a way to target eight different players. Parker Washington is the unquestioned No. 1 receiver in the Jacksonville huddle, but we'd like to see him draw a larger market share.

3. Will Derrick Henry find running lanes? Henry is finally showing some attrition near the end of his Hall of Fame career, sliding down to 4.0 YPC. The loss of Jackson obviously doesn't help, and he'll be challenged by a Jaguars defense that's No. 1 in run defense DVOA. The Ravens would like to give Henry 20 or more touches, and attempt to shorten the game. — Scott Pianowski

Check out more of Scott's work at the Yahoo Sports fantasy hub .

articles.title: Carson Wentz Will Start for Vikings vs. Bills Amid Latest Kyler Murray Injury Timeline Update
articles.summary: The Minnesota Vikings will start Carson Wentz at quarterback in Monday's game against the Buffalo Bills as Kyler Murray deals with a hamstring injury.
articles.body:
The Minnesota Vikings will start Carson Wentz at quarterback in Monday's game against the Buffalo Bills as Kyler Murray deals with a hamstring injury.

Signing Murray to a one-year contract made sense given the paltry cost . The move simply isn't working out.

Since returning from a concussion in Week 3, the two-time Pro Bowler has thrown for 1,004 yards, five touchdowns and two interceptions in five starts. He ranks 26th among qualified players in QBR (44.7) at ESPN.com .

It's getting more and more difficult to maintain hope that Murray can be a successful reclamation project in the vein of Sam Darnold or Baker Mayfield.

Wentz threw for three touchdowns after filling in for Murray in a 39-22 win over the Green Bay Packers, but it was a much different story when he started in Week 2. He went 11-of-20 for 143 yards as Minnesota lost 9-3 to the Chicago Bears.

The fact some would posit the 33-year-old is an upgrade over Murray speaks to how poorly Murray is performing. Wentz is a better pure passer, and that might be enough to make a meaningful difference for the offense.

articles.title: Mike Vrabel's Tom Brady reunion comes with a hilarious twist as Patriots coach jokes about contractual obligation
articles.summary: Mike Vrabel's return to New England has brought plenty of familiar faces back into his orbit, but a reunion with Tom Brady comes with an amusing catch.
articles.body: Mike Vrabel's return to New England has brought plenty of familiar faces back into his orbit, but a reunion with Tom Brady comes with an amusing catch. The exchange also offers a glimpse into the relationship between two figures whose careers remain closely tied to the Patriots' most successful era.Mike Vrabel finds a funny way to describe his Tom Brady reunionMike Vrabel knows what Tom Brady means to the New England Patriots. The two shared the field during one of the most successful periods in franchise history, helping establish a winning culture that defined the organization for nearly two decades.Now, with Vrabel leading the Patriots as head coach, their paths are crossing again. However, his latest comment about meeting Brady added a little humor to the occasion.Rather than making the reunion sound like a major ceremonial moment, Vrabel joked about having a contractual obligation to meet the former quarterback. The remark brought a lighter side to the situation and showed the comfort he has with the people who helped shape his playing career.There is also a deeper connection behind the joke. Vrabel was part of the Patriots' dynasty as a linebacker, while Brady became the central figure of their championship run. They experienced the same demanding environment under Bill Belichick, where preparation, discipline and accountability were expected every day.Their relationship is therefore built on more than shared memories. Both understand what it took to keep New England competitive year after year. Vrabel's return as head coach also gives him a different perspective on the same organization he once helped lead on the field.Brady and Vrabel share a connection that goes beyond New England's dynastyBrady's legacy in New England is difficult to separate from the people who helped build the team's success. Vrabel was one of those players. His contributions on defense played an important role in the Patriots' championship years, and his experience alongside Brady gives their reunion a natural familiarity.But their roles have changed considerably since those playing days. articles.title: New Rumor Suggests NY Giants Being Forced To Wait on Jonathan Taylor Trade Until Specific Date
articles.summary: If the New York Giants are able to complete a blockbuster trade for Jonathan Taylor, a new report suggests it […]
articles.body:
If the New York Giants are able to complete a blockbuster trade for Jonathan Taylor , a new report suggests it will have to wait until just before next week's NFL trade deadline.

This will be an interesting next few days for the Giants. Heading into Sunday's NFL schedule, they own a 4-2-1 record and sit atop the NFC East standings. A year ago, they were 2-5 and considered potential sellers before the deadline. Now they can have reasons to shop for upgrades to make a serious run at the division title in the second half.

The word around the team is that improving the running back room is one of the front office's priorities before Nov. 10. And according to reports over the weekend, the Giants are competing with teams like the Minnesota Vikings and Denver Broncos in the ongoing Taylor sweepstakes.

In a trade deadline report this week, ESPN's Dan Graziano boldly claimed, "I would guess [Taylor] gets traded, and I wouldn't be at all surprised if it was the Giants who made that move ." That is certainly a promising view on Big Blue's chances of acquiring the three-time Pro Bowler. However, if New York can get the deal across the finish line, it won't happen until next week.

Indianapolis Colts holding off on Jonathan Taylor trade until right before the Nov. 10 deadline

"The belief around the league is that, barring an offer that blows them away, Indianapolis plans to wait until after Sunday's game vs. the Dallas Cowboys before revisiting the offers on the table and making the trades that make sense on Monday and Tuesday ahead of the deadline," Jordan Schultz reports.

Reports over the last couple of weeks suggest the Indianapolis Colts want a second-round pick and more in a trade for Taylor. That price could go up if teams are desperate enough to add the 27-year-old still under contract for two more seasons .

According to a previous report from Schultz, a major hurdle for New York to make trades before the deadline is " that the Giants don't have a 4th- or 5th-round pick in 2027 ." They gave up their fifth-rounder in September's JJ McCarthy trade, and their fourth in a deal with the Cleveland Browns last year.

articles.title: Fantasy Football Start 'Em, Sit 'Em: Joel Smyth offers FLEX lineup advice for Quinshon Judkins, Raiders RBs, more players in Week 9
articles.summary: Joel Smyth helps you through those tough flex decisions for your Week 9 fantasy football lineups.
articles.body:
We're on to Week 9 of the fantasy football season! As we look for every advantage this season, the X-Factor position is the FLEX. To break it all down, Yahoo analyst Joel Smyth goes through 8 players in the consensus rankings flex zone for your flexes, double flexes or even third WR slots.

It's time. Jonah Coleman completely took over the backfield in Week 8, handling 11-of-13 carries after J.K. Dobbins opened with the first five. He had five targets, six opportunities at the goal line and a big fantasy day versus a top RB defense. The Panthers, on the other end, just fired their defensive coordinator. Denver, despite a slow start, ranks 10th in RB fantasy points in the first half of the season. With no RJ Harvey, plenty of valuable touches are available to the rookie in a great situation as a whole. Coleman has been the far more successful back and should be treated like such this weekend.

Miami is top-five against wide receivers this season and its passing defense has been terrible. On a per-play basis, the Dolphins rank dead last; they just have not been thrown on much this season. Williams isn't volume dependent, and he may need to hit early on versus the Dolphins to hit at all, but Miami's improvement on offense, paired with the Lions defense, can help.

Over the last month, Miami ranks 14th in scoring offense, which hopefully can keep it close to the powerhouse that is Detroit's offense, entering as touchdown underdogs. Williams' targets aren't always consistent or high, but they have been valuable downfield shots and in the red zone in a top offense, making the overall volume much closer to that of a fantasy WR2 over the last month. He's become a weekly set-and-forget with his production as of late.

With Dylan Sampson back, Judkins becomes much more game-script dependent. That game script has a better shot of staying in his favor this week as 2.5-point underdogs to New Orleans, hopefully a closer game than the 21-point loss to Pittsburgh last weekend. In the Browns' five wins this season, Judkins has scored 14.4 half-PPR PPG, handling an extreme share of the backfield carries and all the goal-line work. The Saints have been an RB's dream so far in 2026, ranking 32nd versus backs on the season, only getting worse over the last five games.​

The Jeanty experience has not been for the faint of heart. What we don't know is how this backfield will be split on the ground this week, the Raiders potentially sticking with Mike Washington Jr. completely, going back to 50-50 or (unlikely) swinging all the way back to Jeanty as the workhorse. What we do know is that there is a 90% chance Jeanty is the receiving back, something that alone would make him the RB22 in PPR scoring, as he's scored the most receiving fantasy points at the position. We also know that, although the 49ers have been the best defense in the NFL versus rushing fantasy points, they also rank 32nd against RB receiving points. I'm not confident if he's my RB1 or RB2, but I still believe he's worthy of a flex spot.​

Maybe give one more week for Odunze. This week I had a personal favorite come out with the Heaven versus Hell Graph , comparing the first half of the season schedule to the second half. Odunze is where you'd want with a much better schedule going forward… after this week. From Weeks 10-17, there isn't a spot you're scared of, but Week 9's matchup versus Tampa Bay isn't ideal.

Odunze will matchup versus Zyon McCollum on nearly half of the plays this Sunday. He's allowing a very low amount of production when targeted against to begin with. The Bucs' defense had been dominant against the pass long before Week 8 versus Atlanta, ranking No. 1 (over Minnesota!) in EPA/pass on the season.

It's been a rollercoaster for Pitts managers; what's new? This week, hopefully it's a game where you don't regret putting him in your lineup the next morning. There's a couple of main reasons why I think Pitts can be used as the extra flex. No. 1, the Bengals. They were horrible against tight ends last year, and are only a little better this season, giving up on average 5.3 PPG more than the average defense does to the position. They struggle up the middle in general and often find themselves in shootouts.

No. 2 is that Cincinnati plays a high amount of man coverage. Pitts is the seventh-best in fantasy points per route this season if he were a WR. For the second straight season, QB Michael Penix Jr. and Pitts have been best buds against man coverage, being the primary reason for most big Pitts days. You won't even need coffee Sunday morning for this game abroad if your heart is already racing with Pitts in the starting lineup.

The stat breaking down the 49ers' running back defense is why Washington is in the booby traps. San Francisco is 32nd versus receiving backs, but first against rushing, where Washington has an extremely low percent (10.8%) of his fantasy points from. If Washington does get the volume again, well, there's a good chance it doesn't work out anyway. The Raiders have converted two of their 17 goal-line carries, which is likely what it would take to overcome the 49ers' rushing defense. The floor is very low for multiple reasons, making it a pass for me until we have more knowledge of the split or at least a better matchup.

Arizona has shockingly not been a positive matchup for running backs this season. The defense is getting scored on more than any team in the NFL, yet they are second-best against RB fantasy points adjusted to the schedule. Charbonnet is coming off of a major injury with multiple other RB options available.

In Week 8, he only played 20-of-57 snaps on offense. It's not enough for me to trust, with around 10 touches being the expected volume. In the past, spots such as these could be salvaged with the goal-line touchdown, which certainly can happen, but a lower shot with the red-zone work being split three ways last week. It's not a guarantee the goal-line carry goes to Charbonnet if there is one at all.

articles.title: Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel Injury Statuses for 49ers vs. Raiders Updated by GM John Lynch
articles.summary: While the San Francisco 49ers are expecting to get back some of their injured wide receivers for Sunday's game against the Las Vegas Raiders, Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel are likely not going to be available.
articles.body:
While the San Francisco 49ers are expecting to get back some of their injured wide receivers for Sunday's game against the Las Vegas Raiders, Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel are likely not going to be available.

Appearing on KNBR's Murph & Markus Show (h/t Matt Maiocco of NBC Sports Bay Area), 49ers general manager John Lynch said the expectation is Evans and Samuel will remain out for Week 9.

Lynch added Demarcus Robinson and KhaDarel Hodge are expected to play against the Raiders.

Evans missed San Francisco's most recent game against the Atlanta Falcons in Week 7 due to Achilles tendinitis. He originally suffered the injury in Week 5 against the Seattle Seahawks.

After trying to play through it the following week against the Washington Commanders, Evans left the field late in the second quarter and didn't return.

Samuel injured his hamstring in the Seahawks game and hasn't played since. Head coach Kyle Shanahan told reporters last week that Samuel and Evans were among a group of players who had a chance to return coming out of the bye.

Despite being without Evans and Samuel for at least one more game, there is good injury news for the 49ers.

Robinson, who has been out since suffering a high-ankle sprain in Week 2, will add much-needed help at wide receiver. He had two catches for 50 yards and a touchdown in the season-opening win against the Los Angeles Rams.

Christian Kirk, Jordan Watkins, Brandin Cooks and Jacob Cowing were the only active wide receivers for the Niners against the Falcons two weeks ago.

In addition to getting Robinson back on offense, the 49ers will get a boost on defense with Nick Bosa planning to play for the first time since Week 2 due to knee and calf issues.

Sunday will also mark the 49ers' first game since acquiring DeForest Buckner, who previously played with San Francisco from 2016 to '19, from the Indianapolis Colts to boost their depth on the interior defensive line.

The 49ers (6-1) are currently the No. 1 seed in the NFC. They will host the Raiders at 4:25 p.m. ET on Sunday.

articles.title: Travis Hunter’s wife Leanna Lenee makes surprising admission about her custom Jaguars outfit before Colts win

articles.body: Travis Hunter’s wife, Leanna Lenee, caught attention with her latest Jacksonville Jaguars game-day look, but wearing the outfit was not as comfortable as it appeared. Ahead of the Jaguars’ November 1 game against the Indianapolis Colts, Leanna put together a custom outfit inspired by the team’s new Rivalries uniforms. She later admitted on TikTok that the look “hurt like heck,” giving fans a glimpse of the effort behind her appearance.Leanna Lenee reveals why her Travis Hunter-inspired Jaguars outfit was uncomfortableLeanna shared an outfit-check video on TikTok, where a fan commented on her game-day look. Responding to the comment, she admitted, “It hurt like heck.” Although she did not explain which part of the outfit caused the discomfort, her video showed the details she had put together for the occasion.Her outfit included a customized, off-the-shoulder Jaguars jersey paired with loose-fitting, leather-style trousers and black heels. She also wore a belly chain with her husband Travis Hunter’s name hanging from it, adding a personal touch to the look. Her accessories included rings, glitter, carefully designed nails and a black handbag.Leanna also shared the fragrance combination she wore for the game. She mixed Valentino Strawberry and Vanilla with YSL Berry to create her own scent for the occasion.However, her preparations were not limited to her own appearance. She also made sure her son had an outfit that matched the family’s Jaguars theme. Since the team did not have the right size available for him, she put together a last-minute combination of a white, black and teal T-shirt, a black jumpsuit and Crocs.This was not Leanna’s first game-day outfit inspired by the Jaguars. During the team’s earlier game against the New England Patriots, she wore a dusty-blue fitted dress decorated with a Jaguars logo, a jaguar patch and a jersey-style number patch. The back also featured Hunter’s name.She completed that look with team-inspired jewellery, a silver Rolex watch and white cowboy boots. Her son joined her in a grey top with Jaguars patches, matching trousers and white shoes.Travis Hunter and Jacksonville Jaguars celebrate 42-7 win over Indianapolis ColtsWhile Leanna was busy putting together her game-day look, Travis Hunter and the Jaguars had an important afternoon on the field. Jacksonville introduced its new Rivalries uniforms against the Colts on November 1 at EverBank Stadium, and the team made the occasion even better with a 42-7 win.The Jaguars had already built a 28-0 lead by halftime, leaving Indianapolis with plenty of work to do after the break. However, Jacksonville continued to control the game and added two more touchdowns in the second half.Hunter had a limited role on offense. He recorded one rushing attempt for five yards and was targeted once but did not make a catch. His defensive numbers were better, as he finished with four tackles, including three solo tackles and one assisted tackle, according to NFL.com.Meanwhile, Trevor Lawrence played a major role in Jacksonville’s win. He completed 10 of 14 passes for 210 yards and three touchdowns without throwing an interception. Running back Bhayshul Tuten also had a strong afternoon, finishing with 104 rushing yards and a touchdown on 16 carries. He added two catches for 55 yards and another touchdown.Jacksonville’s defense also made life difficult for the Colts, forcing three turnovers during the game. The result gave the Jaguars another important divisional win.For Leanna, the afternoon was also an opportunity to support her husband and his team through a carefully planned family look. Although she admitted that her outfit was painful to wear, she still gave fans a closer look at the work that went into getting ready for the game.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Indianapolis Colts star Jonathan Taylor is tuning out the steady drumbeat of rumors about his future with the team.
articles.body:
Indianapolis Colts star Jonathan Taylor is tuning out the steady drumbeat of rumors about his future with the team.

Taylor addressed whether he has requested a trade ahead of the deadline when speaking to reporters Thursday. He also called the rumors "noise," pointing out how the saga has been "dragging on for a while now":

It's not a foregone conclusion the three-time Pro Bowler is moved before the Nov. 10 trade deadline. But the Colts are open for business after trading away Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner.

NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported Indy could wait until after Week 9's games before making a final decision on its best remaining trade assets.

Ian Rapoport of NFL Network offered a similar narrative:

Taylor is signed for two more years, and he's putting together a solid season so far. He has run for 610 yards and eight touchdowns while averaging 4.1 yards per carry.

If the Colts think they can make a quick turnaround in 2027, then holding onto Taylor makes sense. That's the approach the Philadelphia Eagles are taking with their star running back, Saquon Barkley.

When Taylor's value may never be higher, holding onto him through the deadline is less logical if ownership is ready for a full rebuild. Fans will also read between the lines with his vague response to a direct question about a trade request.

Maybe the Colts stand pat. It feels like a scenario where they'll wait as long as they can to see if anybody will increase their bid. Then they'll settle for the best offer on the table.

articles.title: Week 9 Start 'Em, Sit 'Em, Play or Bench Tips for Fantasy Football Managers
articles.summary: Week 9 will open with Thursday night's matchup between the Baltimore Ravens and Jacksonville Jaguars. It will culminate with a Monday night showdown between the Buffalo Bills and Minnesota Vikings. In between will be a 13-game Sunday slate that will test the nerves of many a fantasy football manager.
articles.body:
Week 9 will open with Thursday night's matchup between the Baltimore Ravens and Jacksonville Jaguars. It will culminate with a Monday night showdown between the Buffalo Bills and Minnesota Vikings. In between will be a 13-game Sunday slate that will test the nerves of many a fantasy football manager.

This season has been wildly unpredictable in the world of fantasy, and things are unlikely to change in Week 9. Only the Pittsburgh Steelers and Tennessee Titans are on bye, but injuries continue to impact most teams.

Here, you'll find some start/sit recommendations for second-tier starters based on recent performances, projected roles, individual matchups, and point-per-reception (PPR) scoring.

Start: Matthew Stafford, Los Angeles Rams

The Los Angeles Rams still aren't looking like the Super Bowl favorites they were touted as heading into the season. However, they have won two in a row and have seen their offense chug along without Davante Adams.

The play of quarterback Matthew Stafford has helped to put L.A. back in the playoff picture, and it should allow the Rams to thrive against the Washington Commanders this week.

Washington has actually been fairly solid against the run this season. However, it has surrendered the fifth-most fantasy points to opposing quarterbacks.

Carolina Panthers quarterback Bryce Young has been a strong streamer for most of this season. However, his offensive line is banged-up and becoming more of a liability by the week.

As a result, Young has tallied just 18.8 fantasy points over the past two weeks combined.

Things won't get any easier this week against a potent Denver Broncos pass rush. The Broncos have been fairly average against QBs in fantasy (14th-most points allowed), but it's impossible to trust Carolina's O-line here.

Christian McCaffrey, San Francisco 49ers

Start: Rhamondre Stevenson, New England Patriots

The New England Patriots are coming off a surprisingly tough win over the rival Miami Dolphins. The game required a second-half comeback, which limited running back Rhamondre Stevenson—though he still finished with 12 fantasy points.

Stevenson should have a much bigger game this week against the visiting Green Bay Packers. Keeping the Packers offense off the field will be a priority, and Stevenson should get a ton of work with TreVeyon Henderson battling an ankle sprain.

The Packers have surrendered the eighth-most fantasy points to opposing RBs this season.

While the Patriots fell behind early in Miami, they did a solid job of limiting budding star back Ollie Gordon II. The Dolphins' new starter rushed for just 69 yards and 3.6 yards per carry.

This week, Miami is likely to test a suspect Detroit Lions pass defense early and often. That doesn't bode well for Gordon, who has just six receptions in seven games.

The Lions have surrendered the fourth-fewest fantasy points to opposing RBs. Gordon should see the bench this week, along with the following backs:

Start: Matthew Golden, Green Bay Packers

The Green Bay Packers will face a pretty solid overall New England Patriots defense this week. However, Green Bay's ground game continues to be stuck in neutral. No. 1 wideout Christian Watson is also dealing with a broken rib and is likely to draw the attention of New England's secondary—which has been average in terms of fantasy limitations.

The Patriots have surrendered the 11th-most fantasy points to opposing receivers.

All of this lays the foundation for a potentially huge day by budding star Matthew Golden, who is coming off a 20.9-point outing.

Panthers receiver Jalen Coker has cooled off considerably in recent weeks. He has failed to reach double-digit fantasy points in three of his last four games and has fallen short of five points in two of those contests.

Carolina's issues along the offensive line won't help Coker against a solid Broncos secondary this week.

The Panthers should lean heavily on their ground game, limiting Coker's ability to generate big plays or record a high volume of targets. Denver has surrendered the sixth-fewest fantasy points to opposing WRs.

Start: T.J. Hockenson, Minnesota Vikings

Quarterback Kyler Murray has not experienced the career renaissance with the Minnesota Vikings that many expected. He has, however, developed a strong rapport with tight end T.J. Hockenson, especially recently.

Hockenson has topped 13 fantasy points in each of his last two outings, and he should reach double digits again this week. The Buffalo Bills have been average against opposing TEs (11 points per game allowed), but they also have an offense that can put up points in bunches.

Even with an elite defense, the Vikings may have to chase points via the pass this week. That puts Hockenson firmly in must-start territory.

While the Bills may find ways to cut through Minnesota's defense on Monday night, they're unlikely to do it with tight end Dalton Kincaid. The Vikings have a terrific group of safeties and linebackers that have regularly shut down opposing tight ends.

No team has surrendered fewer fantasy points (5.5 per game) to opposing tight ends this season.

Sitting Kincaid will be difficult after last week's 18.6-point outing. Managers with other options at TE, though, should take them.

*Fantasy scoring information from FantasyPros .

articles.title: Brandon Aiyuk's 49ers Future Addressed by John Lynch After WR Applies for NFL Reinstatement
articles.summary: San Francisco 49ers general manager John Lynch was tight-lipped about the team's plan for Brandon Aiyuk after the veteran wide receiver applied for reinstatement on Wednesday following an 11-month stint on the reserve/left squad list.
articles.body:
San Francisco 49ers general manager John Lynch was tight-lipped about the team's plan for Brandon Aiyuk after the veteran wide receiver applied for reinstatement on Wednesday following an 11-month stint on the reserve/left squad list.

Appearing on KNBR's Murph & Markus show (h/t Harrison Rich of the San Francisco Chronicle ), Lynch said the situation with Aiyuk remains "fluid" and all options remain on the table:

"I'm gonna kind of leave it at that, because I've been recommended to do so, and I think it's the right thing to do. We'll look for a pathway for both sides here that works. ... I think everything's possible. I will say this: We've worked with (agent Drew Rosenhaus) a lot. Drew is a good guy to deal with. He's reasonable, he's got integrity. … We'll see how this thing goes. I think I'll just leave it at that."

Aiyuk hired Drew Rosenhaus as his new agent earlier this week after firing his previous representation in November 2025.

Rosenhaus' first move was to apply for reinstatement on Aiyuk's behalf in order to help him get back to the NFL. Aiyuk is scheduled to report to the 49ers' facilities on Friday.

Assuming Aiyuk does appear at the facilities, it will mark his first time back in the building with the Niners since sometime in 2025. He had been rehabbing a knee injury suffered midway through the 2024 season with the expectation he would return to play at some point.

However, in November 2025, it was reported the 49ers were voiding the remaining guaranteed money on Aiyuk's contract because he had gone months without attending meetings or taking part in other team activities.

The following month, Aiyuk was placed on the reserve/left squad list . Lynch and head coach Kyle Shanahan have given no indication they would bring him back into the fold amid this ongoing saga.

Shanahan told reporters on Wednesday he has "no expectation" for Aiyuk's return to the facilities and he has "moved on mentally" from the entire situation.

Since Aiyuk has been on the reserve/left squad list, he does not count against the 49ers' roster or salary cap. If he ends up being released, the Niners would take on a $31.6 million dead-cap hit between 2026 and '27.

Aiyuk played a total of seven games after signing a four-year, $120 million extension with San Francisco in August 2024. The 28-year-old had back-to-back 1,000-yard seasons in 2022 and '23.

articles.title: Bill Belichick Among Pro Football Hall of Fame's Class of 2027 HC Candidates After 2026 Snub
articles.summary: Six-time Super Bowl-winning head coach Bill Belichick will get a second crack at enshrinement into the Pro Football Hall of Fame.
articles.body:
Six-time Super Bowl-winning head coach Bill Belichick will get a second crack at enshrinement into the Pro Football Hall of Fame.

Belichick is one of five nominees in the coach category for the 2027 class. The other four are Tom Coughlin, Mike Holmgren, Dan Reeves and Mike Shanahan.

Fans were stunned when Belichick was passed over during his first year of Hall of Fame eligibility. He's one of the greatest coaches in NFL history and is third all time in wins.

The explanation for his snub was pretty benign .

Seemingly enough voters independently thought Belichick would sail through, so they strategically picked other candidates who were on the bubble. As a result, the person with the strongest resume didn't move on to the next phase.

The Hall of Fame amended its voting procedures in an effort to avoid a similar situation in the future.

For retired coaches, one of the five nominees advances to the final stage. Under the Hall of Fame's bylaws, voters have to select between three and seven new members from the 15-person finalist pool, which includes 13 players and one contributor.

Belichick will be the heavy favorite to make it through, which is tough because the other four all have good cases for themselves.

Reeves took the Denver Broncos to the Super Bowl three times between 1986-89 and then won an NFC title with the Atlanta Falcons in 1998. He ranks 12th in wins.

Coughlin won a pair of Super Bowls with the New York Giants and turned the Jacksonville Jaguars into a playoff team in just their second year of existence.

Holmgren is another Super Bowl champion with two additional NFC titles. He also produced quite a coaching tree during his 17 years as a head coach.

Shanahan helped popularize the zone blocking scheme , which he used to great effect with the Denver Broncos. He was also responsible for John Elway finally getting over the hump and wrapping up his career with back-to-back Super Bowl wins.

As much as those four achieved, it's difficult to picture Belichick missing out for a second straight year.

articles.title: El Bernabéu ya está listo para la NFL: "Es un estadio más americano que europeo"
articles.standfirst: MARCA ha tenido acceso al interior del recinto en la previa del encuentro entre los Atlanta Falcons y los Cincinnati Bengals
articles.summary: MARCA ha tenido acceso al interior del recinto en la previa del encuentro entre los Atlanta Falcons y los Cincinnati Bengals
articles.body: Es difícil imaginar líneas blancas cada diez yardas y el escudo de la NFL en el centro del campo del Santiago Bernabéu. Pero así es como se presenta el recinto madridista hoy en día. El templo blanco acogerá este domingo el encuentro entre los Atlanta Falcons y los Cincinnati Bengals, y ya está vestido para la ocasión. Este será el segundo encuentro que disputará la NFL en España y contará con las mejores estrellas de la liga: Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase o Bijan Robinson. MARCA ha tenido la oportunidad de acceder al estadio del Real Madrid en la previa del encuentro. Un estadio que ha sufrido una transformación por completo y que ha pasado de ser un terreno de 'soccer' a uno de fútbol americano. Todo ello, de la mano de Nick Pappas, director de campo de la NFL: "En cada estadio aprendemos cosas nuevas y vamos mejorando determinados aspectos. Hemos trabajado muy duro para conseguir que todo saliera bien. Nos sentimos seguros de que podíamos aplicar el mismo esfuerzo y el mismo procedimiento que utilizamos entonces para preparar el terreno de juego. Evidentemente, hay otros aspectos del estadio y de las instalaciones que quizá hayan necesitado algunos pequeños ajustes, pero nosotros hemos podido mantener el mismo plan que teníamos previsto el año pasado". En lo relativo al recinto en su conjunto, Pappas considera que no tiene nada que envidiar a alguno de la NFL: "Es un estadio más americano que europeo. La renovación y las mejoras son espectaculares: la posibilidad de contar con un techo, la enorme pantalla que tenemos sobre nosotros. Es el tipo de instalaciones que vemos en muchos de los estadios nuevos que se construyen en Estados Unidos. Muchos de los estadios a los que acudimos son más tradicionales, quizá más antiguos, al estilo de los estadios europeos. Todos tienen sus particularidades y aspectos positivos. Pero este estadio es una auténtica maravilla de la ingeniería". La primera transformación que ha sufrido el estadio se encuentra en el terreno de juego. Cuando se prepara un campo de fútbol americano, el terreno de juego de fútbol convencional se queda corto, aunque tiene anchura suficiente, por eso se debe llevar a cabo una ampliación del campo. "Este campo tiene la anchura necesaria para el fútbol americano, pero no la longitud, así que tuvimos que añadir aproximadamente seis metros en cada extremo. Las gradas están muy cerca del terreno de juego, así que, para conseguir la longitud que necesitamos, primero hay que retirar las primeras filas de asientos. Después, ampliamos el terreno de juego desde el césped existente hasta llegar a la zona donde estaban esas primeras filas. Colocamos el césped hasta una determinada distancia y, más allá de las líneas que delimitan el campo, instalamos césped artificial alrededor de todo el perímetro exterior", explica Nick Pappas. Una vez llevado a cabo este proceso, empiezan con las marcas reglamentarias de competición: las líneas que delimitan el terreno de juego, las zonas interiores y exteriores, todas las líneas cada cinco yardas, los números y las marcas transversales que se pueden ver sobre el césped. Después llegan los colores más llamativos, que normalmente corresponden a la imagen corporativa de los equipos. En este caso, tenemos a los Cincinnati Bengals en una de las zonas de anotación y a los Atlanta Falcons en la otra. En el centro del campo siempre se coloca el escudo de la NFL. Este proceso continuará durante todo el viernes. El sábado irán algunos representantes de los equipos para conocer el terreno de juego, recorrerlo, visitar sus vestuarios y hacer una visita guiada por el estadio. Finalmente, todo estará preparado para el día del partido, el domingo por la mañana. Sobre el césped en sí, surge la duda de si el partido se disputará en el mismo tapete sobre el que juega el Real Madrid. Y la respuesta es sí: "Podemos disputar nuestros partidos aquí por varias razones. Aunque nuestros deportes son bastante diferentes y nuestros deportistas también, el Real Madrid, en el fútbol, presta muchísima atención al comportamiento del balón sobre el terreno de juego. Es fundamental que el balón ruede con suavidad y que el bote sea el adecuado. El Real Madrid cuenta con un terreno de juego híbrido. Es decir, está compuesto principalmente por césped natural, combinado con algunas fibras que aportan durabilidad, resistencia y tracción para los deportistas. Es una instalación realmente impresionante". El director de campo ha hablado sobre las dificultades que afronta el césped del estadio blanco: "Aunque cuando la gente ve todos los recursos y medios disponibles puede pensar que resulta fácil mantener el césped en estas condiciones, creo que es importante entender que para el equipo que trabaja aquí se trata de un entorno extremadamente complicado. El césped necesita crecer y depende de elementos naturales como el sol, el aire y las temperaturas exteriores. El equipo tiene que trabajar para conseguir que todo funcione correctamente y garantizar que la superficie de juego esté en unas condiciones excelentes. Es un trabajo realmente complicado. Todo está controlado mediante sistemas de climatización. Pueden regular la temperatura, la cantidad de luz, el espectro lumínico y el tiempo de exposición a la luz. Realmente es una instalación única en el mundo. Existen otros terrenos de juego especiales en diferentes lugares, pero no hay nada comparable a esto". Los vestuarios también sufren una transformación importante, entre otras cosas, por la cantidad de personas que tienen que acoger. La diferencia entre el fútbol y el fútbol americano es que, probablemente, un equipo de fútbol tiene unas 25 personas, mientras que en la NFL viajan más de 100 personas, de las cuales aproximadamente 60 son jugadores: "Necesitamos tres vestuarios, que intentamos proporcionar para que los equipos puedan prepararse y entrenar. Hemos añadido aseos, duchas y salas para los entrenadores, ya que estos disponen de una sala independiente. También aprovechamos los espacios adicionales que hay alrededor de las instalaciones". El vestuario de los Bengals, que juegan como visitantes, será el del Real Madrid, con un bloque de taquillas añadidos para la gente. Los Falcons usarán de vestuario una sala adicional con una distribución rectangular, que se parece más a lo que se suele encontrar en otros estadios: muchas taquillas en el centro y una sala bastante grande.
