articles.title: Shedeur Sanders Hyped by Browns WR Before Potential Start vs. Saints Amid Watson Injury, 'Baller'
articles.summary: The Cleveland Browns feel like they will be in good hands if second-year quarterback Shedeur Sanders has to start Sunday's game against the New Orleans Saints.
articles.body:
The Cleveland Browns feel like they will be in good hands if second-year quarterback Shedeur Sanders has to start Sunday's game against the New Orleans Saints.

After veteran signal-caller Deshaun Watson was placed in concussion protocol on Tuesday, Sanders' teammates are confident that he could lead them to success if called upon.

"Just his competitive nature, man, his big-play ability, the way he drives the ball downfield, gives the receiver chances and just make plays," Browns receiver Jerry Jeudy said, per Mary Kay Cabot of Cleveland.com. "He's a baller, man."

Sanders briefly saw the field in Sunday's 27-6 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers. The 24-year-old played in eight games as a rookie and threw for 1,400 yards, seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions on his way to being named to the Pro Bowl as an alternate.

At 5-3, the Browns are still in a position to fight for an AFC North title in a year when they were expected to be rebuilding. If Sanders starts Sunday against New Orleans (2-5), Cleveland will be confident that he can steady the ship until Watson returns.

articles.title: Matthew Stafford, Sean Payton, Mike Macdonald Headline 2026 NFL Salute to Service Award Finalists
articles.summary: Three different Super Bowl champions headline the list of finalists for the 2026 NFL Salute to Service Award presented by USAA.
articles.body:
Three different Super Bowl champions headline the list of finalists for the 2026 NFL Salute to Service Award presented by USAA.

Los Angeles Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford, Denver Broncos head coach Sean Payton and Seattle Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald are all finalists for the annual award. Each team has a finalist for the award that recognizes those who support the military community

Here is a look at the full list of finalists.

Fans will have the opportunity to vote on the winner by visiting NFL.com/SaluteFanVote . That voting will help decide the three finalists, and the winner will be named at NFL Honors during the week of Super Bowl LXI in Los Angeles.

The fans aren't the only ones who will have a say in the winner, as San Francisco 49ers star running back Christian McCaffrey is joining the Salute to Service Award panel that will decide the winner.

McCaffrey took home the award last year thanks to the Christian McCaffrey Foundation's 23 and Troops initiative that provides athlete-level physical and mental care for the military community.

USAA will donate $25,000 in honor of this year's winner to official aid societies, while the NFL Foundation will match the contribution to the winner's military nonprofit charity of choice.

While it remains to be seen who will take home the award this season, Stafford, Payton and Macdonald are headline names.

Stafford has supported the military community in a number of ways, including through his support for the Rams' military flag football tournament and by hosting those preparing to enlist in the military and presenting them with the opportunity to be recognized on the field.

He and his wife, Kelly, also worked with the Rams to help create "Honor Row," which was used to recognize Navy SEALS during one of the team's home games. Stafford also supported the American Red Cross' Holiday Mail for Heroes campaign and even appeared on a holiday card.

As for Payton, whose father served in the military, his advocacy includes supporting K9s for Warriors. Payton has supported the organization that pairs veterans with trained service dogs to help with mental health dating back to 2013 through the funding of training for a number of dogs.

The Broncos head coach also used his Play It Forward Foundation to raise more than $200,000 for veteran programs and established a partnership between the team and K9s for Warriors to help Colorado veterans in particular.

Macdonald's father also served in the armed forces, and the Seahawks head coach supports the military community in a number of ways.

He brought the team to Joint Base Lewis-McChord to visit with service members, welcomed more than 50 Navy sailors and leaders to Seahawks practice, and even brought the U.S. Navy Blue Angels to speak with his team.

articles.title: “I know it doesn’t last forever”: Patrick Mahomes opens up about how he could miss watching his children grow up
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes, the Kansas City Chiefs’ top quarterback, has remained committed to his career on the field as the team has suffered back to back losses
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes, the Kansas City Chiefs’ top quarterback, has remained committed to his career on the field as the team has suffered back to back losses on the field in the last week. As the team is focused on bouncing back on the field, Patrick Mahomes has opened up about how fatherhood has inspired him to balance things better in his life.Patrick Mahomes reflects on what fatherhood has taught him about his career as he remains a dedicated fatherIn an interview, the three time Super Bowl Most Valuable Patrick Mahomes has opened up about life as he said, “I think now, being able to go home and see my daughter and see my son, I have a better understanding of being present and enjoying it…”Patrick Mahomes added, “That translates to the football field, and we’ve been on a heck of a run, but I’m trying to enjoy those moments because I know it doesn’t last forever even though we want it to.”Patrick Mahomes also reflected on how he has taken advice from the NFL legend Peyton Manning as he said, “I actually talked to Peyton about it for a while…What stuck with me is he said, ‘At the end of my career, I wish I would have done it, so my kids could’ve seen what I was doing every day.'”The star player added, “When my kids grow up, I wanted them to see that dad wasn’t just gone just to be gone. I was gone doing something, to build, to be great. And so, whenever they get older, they can see how hard I worked.”Ever since Patrick Mahomes became a father in 2021, he has been dedicated to being present for all of his three children.Both Patrick Mahomes and his wife, Brittany Mahomes, have always prioritized their children and have stayed away from any controversial drama or comments.Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes are often trolled for their marriage and commitment to one anotherWhile they remain committed to the family they have created, things have not been that easy for either of them.Patrick Mahomes might be one of the greatest quarterbacks in the league but he has faced his fair share of criticism. articles.title: 2027 NFL Draft: Top 50 big board 2.0 delivers big changes at quarterback
articles.summary: Eric Edholm's top 50 prospects for the 2027 NFL Draft, from the incomparable Jeremiah Smith down to a rising LB.
articles.body:
My first version of the Big Board , which dropped in early September, was capped at 30 prospects. With more than half the college football season in the books, we've expanded the list on our second edition to 50 prospects — and there has been a lot of change.

Quarterback is a position that has seen significant change, with what was billed as a potentially generational QB crop turning into a semi-disappointing one. That said, a few new names have emerged there, and it's hardly a total loss.

Other positions where there has been noticeable change include offensive tackle and defensive tackle, with a few out-of-nowhere prospects zooming up the list.

Plenty will change between now and April. For now, here are my top 50 prospects for the 2027 NFL Draft as we enter the home stretch of the college football season.

Smith is one of the best wide receiver prospects to come around in recent years, and I expect him to be the highest-drafted non-quarterback next spring, perhaps even going first overall. Keyshawn Johnson in 1996 was the last WR selected No. 1 overall. It has been a disappointing turn of events with QB Julian Sayin's injury, but Smith has continued executing at a high level.

Moore doesn't have an interception this season, but he has four passes defended and only seven passes allowed on 16 attempts in 2026. He's a Pat Surtain II-Sauce Gardner level prospect who can make an instant impact as a rookie next NFL season.

Stewart's return from suspension has led to some promising developments. He's seen an uptick in snaps and is back to flashing a remarkable get-off. Tools-wise, there are few better defensive prospects than this Brian Burns-ian rusher. Is Stewart finally ready to put it all together?

Becker has expanded his role this season amid QB play that hasn't come close to Fernando Mendoza's level from a year ago. His length, body control, vertical speed and exceptional hands will serve him well in the NFL. With Indiana on the ropes against Minnesota, Becker made two clutch catches late to help win.

Mestemaker has seized the opportunity to claim the top slot among draft QB prospects in what has been a tough start to the season at quarterback. He's a fearless gunner who can manufacture drives with arm, athleticism and creativity but also stunt them with some shaky decision-making.

A high-ankle sprain has sidelined Simmons for the time being, but it's not expected to be a season-ending injury. His production to date dwarfs that of Stewart, but in a traits-over-production league, Stewart rates as a bit more rare.

Clemson's season has been a disappointment, but Hampton has not. After some great reps against Miami's Malachi Toney, the best receiver not named Jeremiah Smith, Hampton looked the part of a possible top-10 pick. He's very well built, and a strong 40-yard dash time could land him very high in the draft.

Echoles' performance against LSU was the kind of tape you could hold up and slap a top-10 grade on. He's been good otherwise, but not at that same dominant level since. Echoles finished strong last season, and I am hoping for a similar flourish to this season to justify a top-10 grade.

Seaton's pass-blocking potential might exceed any other OT prospect in this class, but he's far from perfect. There are questions about his run blocking and pad level, but Seaton's athleticism and quick reaction skills are strong.

Cole ran back a 66-yard fumble return for a TD last week vs. Florida and had an 85-yard scoop-and-score earlier in the season. He's not on the Sonny Styles spectrum of freaky athlete, but Cole isn't far behind. He could have a Roquan Smith-like career and impact on a defense and is ascending quickly.

Gilliam has been one of the bigger risers in the 2027 class and could profile as a Byron Murphy II-like rusher in this class. With a stocky frame, low center of gravity and unusual explosiveness, Gilliam could be a disruptive 3-technique for a slanting front.

Chambliss is already fighting age and size questions, and his play hasn't been close to flawless, with a pattern of starting games slowly before settling in. But he has inherent playmaking traits you can't find in most quarterbacks, a knack for big plays in big games and the ability to create out of structure, putting the whole field in play with his arm talent and athleticism. I'm still buying stock.

Coleman's upside remains elite, but he hasn't put it all together for various reasons. He's been a bit banged up, and Texas' offense has held him back surprisingly. Coleman has still flashed high-end ability in his age-20 season.

Baugh's size-speed profile is top notch, with quick burst and acceleration for such a big back. He can power through contact and also pick his way through small gaps, with shades of Le'Veon Bell as a runner. Baugh's long speed is just ordinary, and I'm not as sold on his three-down ability. He's the best back in this class but perhaps not a generational prospect.

There might be more worry when he arrives in the NFL, but Robinson's leaner frame (180-ish pounds) hasn't held him back in college. He's tough, competitive, always around the ball and plays physically, willing to tackle and mix it up with receivers, even if that can lead to flags.

I underrated Johnson coming into the season, and he's been a big part of the Gophers' success, shifting to center out of necessity the past few games. That likely won't be his NFL position, but he's played all five OL spots in college, combining a good anchor with great size and fairly quick feet.

Pierre is not a refined pass rusher yet, and he lacks elite edge bend. But his game has expanded this season. He's making an impact in coverage, as a run stopper and rushing the passer. He can play in a two-point stance and profiles well for an odd-front defense.

Manning's season hasn't gone as expected, but it's not as if he's turned into some unskilled stiff. Scouts still like the tools and traits, but executing the mundane stuff hasn't come as readily in Year 4 at Texas. He could still declare, but NFL people believe a return to college — though maybe not at Texas — is a real possibility.

Heard has been another OT riser who has benefitted from a new scenery, displaying greater pass-blocking potential with the Wildcats than he did at Tennessee. Heard uses his broad frame and finisher's mentality to bury people in the run game. If he can tighten up against quicker speed rushers, Heard could be a top-20 pick.

I've held back ranking Simmons until now, similar to how I slow-played Ty Simpson a year ago, because of his lack of experience. However, in a QB class that has been disappointing on the whole, Simmons is among the clear winners. He's as pretty a thrower as there is in college football, capable of hitting just about anything anywhere when he's on schedule and the protection holds up. Under pressure is where things get a murky, but Simmons is a talent worth investing in.

I was a bit higher on Goosby than Jordan Seaton coming into the season, but Goosby hadn't dominated early in the season prior to a season-ending knee injury that has left his draft stock in question. He will have a decision on coming out, which is complicated by a 6-to-9-month rehab, and could return to school.

Mensah lacks elite traits, but his production and execution speak for themselves. He'll be appealing to QB-needy teams because of his maturity, unusual accuracy and ability to consume a lot mentally. The showdown against CJ Carr and Notre Dame will be prime scouting tape.

One of the big risers to this point of the season, Williams was a virtual unknown outside of the Utes' program toiling for the prior two seasons as OT3 behind 2026 first-rounders Spencer Fano and Caleb Lomu. Williams' reach, leg drive and good balance are all great traits for a nearly 6-foot-8 blocker, but his pad level and short pass sets can sometimes hinder Williams.

Thompkins has been just as impactful on Bama's defense as Yhonzae Pierre this season, providing solid run defense and pressure on passing downs. He's been a better player than he was at USC and has versatility, lining up at multiple spots. A former high school hoops standout, Thompkins is a 6-5, 290-plus pound athlete who's just starting to tap into his football prowess.

Carr is another QB prospect who has helped his chances of draft success, be it this year or next. His pedestrian schedule is a talking point, but we'll see Carr against Miami — a key battle that could have a big say on whether he comes out or stays in school.

Johnson has been held back by his team's offensive struggles, and he's not the most dynamic athlete, but he's got an NFL-ready frame and natural receiving ability to be a red-zone and middle-field threat. Johnson is very polished as an all-around tight end.

It's hard to know where to slot Moore, who is out of eligibility and reportedly will be shut down for the season. His draft stock has taken a hit amid a slow start to the season, followed by a concussion, and Moore isn't likely to go as high as he would have in the 2026 draft. Yet, he still could be a first-round pick.

A long, press corner, Jones won't be for every team or scheme. There's some stiffness in his hips, struggling to handle quicker receivers, but Jones' length and press-man ability will be valued by teams such as the Browns and Patriots that run a lot of man coverage.

Green's knee injury in Week 3 against Ole Miss sidelined him for multiple weeks but he has since reprised his role as the Tigers' do-it-all star. He can line up in-line, flexed to the slot or in the backfield. He could stand to add mass and strength on his 6-foot-7 frame.

Pieper is playing out of position at right guard. His best NFL position figures to be center, but Pieper has hardly played there at Iowa. He's a very good athlete in a smaller frame (6-foot-3, 298 pounds), and length will give him problems, but his pulling and climbing ability will make him a fit in a zone-blocking scheme.

Lord knows I've fallen for some bigger wide receivers who flopped in the NFL, but I just can't quit Duff. He lacks suddenness off the line and out of his breaks, but Duff's body control, big frame (6-foot-6, 225 pounds), speed (for his size) and his my-ball attitude are all great traits. He can feast on slants and fades in the NFL.

Marsh has flashed in two big areas since arriving at Indiana: blocking and yards after the catch. His effort as a run blocker hasn't gone unnoticed among scouts, and he's been excellent with the ball in his hands in the open field. His separation ability reads as average, but Marsh is a thick-framed receiver with juice.

Lauck's arm length could end up putting him in the guard discussion once he's measured at the scouting combine, but his technique as a leverage blocker should allow him to be successful. He's a good athlete with a higher floor.

Bolden getting hurt (and playing hurt) has dinged his draft stock a smidge, but scouts have noted his toughness and love his mentality, even with a smaller frame (6-foot, 190 pounds) more prone to injury. He's still a potential rookie starter for me, depending on where he lands.

With an elite size-speed-power profile, Washington should have a high draft floor. There are only so many men on the planet this size (6-foot-3, 325 pounds) and movement ability. He'll make you think twice about running through the B-gap, but Washington's pass-rush appeal is limited to bull rushes and closing down passing lanes.

One Texas player who seemingly has helped his draft cause this season has been Siani, who combines light feet with great length and movement skills. A late bloomer who grew up playing soccer (including as a goalkeeper) in Canada, Siani has had a few forgettable reps vs. better players, but he has experience at both OT spots and has upside.

I've been a little disappointed in Stone this season, but perhaps he's been playing in pain after a September knee injury. Because of the relative lack of DT depth, Stone's tools still could serve him well come draft time if he declares. He's toolsy and explosive but also unrefined.

Smith has more than 3,000 college snaps at left tackle and was an underrated cog on last year's national title team. Some NFL teams view him more as a guard at the next level, but he should have fairly broad appeal at either spot considering Smith's intellect, savvy handwork and good-enough anchor.

Heldt has three sacks in his past two games, and his pressure rates have been consistently good this season after a poor showing Week 1 vs. LSU. He might never be a true edge bender, but Heldt is a high-effort defender with great length.

His production is back to freshman-year level, and Coleman-Williams seemingly has kicked the drops problem he suffered as a sophomore. He's an electric, shifty receiver whose game still needs fine-tuning, but the arrow is pointed up again.

Traore was ejected for a dirty hit on BYU's Bear Bachmeier, which cost the Irish dearly, but Traore has been one of Notre Dame's best all-around players this season. He's an extremely well-built athlete with length and a hot motor. He'll get a terrific test Saturday vs. Miami.

Scott remains a tools-over-production prospect now, and he needs a better plan when his initial rush is stalled, but he's a quality athlete who works well laterally to make plays and can beat guards with quickness.

Alexander is a leaner-framed receiver who wins with speed, route tempo and body control. He hasn't been as effective as a deep-ball threat this season, but Alexander has the juice to ignite an offense.

He's cooled off after a blistering start (five INTs in his first three games), and Lopa could return to college in 2027. His traits, however, are very unusual; you don't see 6-foot-5, 210-pound safeties who can move like he does.

Brown was knocked out of the Tennessee game a few weeks ago and hasn't played since but is on track to return soon, perhaps even vs. LSU this weekend. He's a physical, field-fast corner with loose hips and good man-coverage technique. He will, however, lose some battles to more physically gifted receivers and hasn't been a huge playmaker this season.

Lacy has been beset by injuries this season and could miss some time with the dislocated shoulder he suffered against Texas. When healthy, he's a bursty runner with strong contact balance and big-play ability. His heavy workload in 2025 may have had a negative effect.

47. Kyngstonn Viliamu-Asa, LB, Notre Dame

He's a little less than a year removed from his second torn ACL in his left knee, but it appears that Viliamu-Asa has maintained his speed. KVA has missed time this season with a thumb injury, and the medical portion will be big on his evaluation, but he has flashed major talent in a smaller sample size.

Swain has had a few hiccups this season, just as his former running mate Brandon Cisse did a year ago. But I am betting on athletic traits and Swain's competitive style, both of which are NFL-caliber. He's also a terrific punt returner.

If you're looking for a true center-fielder type with range and instincts, McClain is your guy. He should run well, has adequate size and could rise with more plays on the ball.

After a few incomplete seasons at Oklahoma, Omosigho has emerged as the heartbeat of a UCLA defense that has allowed 35 points in its past seven games. He's a thick-bodied, do-it-all defender who has made an impact as a pass rusher, run stopper and in coverage.

articles.title: Jared Verse Calls Out 'Dirty S--t' from Steelers OL, Says He's 'Upset' with Browns Teammates
articles.summary: Cleveland Browns edge-rusher Jared Verse took exception to his teammates' reaction after he was slammed to the turf in the 27-6 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers.
articles.body:
Cleveland Browns edge-rusher Jared Verse took exception to his teammates' reaction after he was slammed to the turf in the 27-6 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers.

During one point-after attempt, Steelers guard Mason McCormick had Verse mid-air and forcefully pushed him down. Verse not only described that as "dirty s--t" but also said he expected his teammates to come to his defense:

Steelers safety Jaquan Brisker told reporters following the game the two-time Pro Bowler "should have kept his mouth shut" after dishing out some trash talk when the Browns beat Pittsburgh earlier this year.

Verse said that's just his nature, and he believes he performs better when there's a "personal" edge:

In a rivalry game like this, neither team needs any additional motivation. Verse supplied some anyway when he suggested the Browns were going to "make Pittsburgh ours on Sunday."

That obviously didn't happen, and the Steelers offensive line kept Verse in check. He was limited to one total tackle.

Browns coach Todd Monken didn't call out any specific players but made some pointed comments in the aftermath.

"We weren't very poised and we didn't keep our composure," he told reporters Monday. "And you are how you play, not how you talk. And that was the message all week. It'll continue to be our message each week. And that is 'speak with your play.' I'll leave it at that."

Verse is in his first year with Cleveland after coming over in the Myles Garrett trade. He remains without a sack through eight games.

articles.title: New Jets Trade Rumors Update Breece Hall Talks Ahead of 2026 NFL Deadline
articles.summary: With the NFL Trade Deadline just under a week away, and it remains to be seen if the New York Jets will trade off any of their pieces.
articles.body:
With the NFL Trade Deadline just under a week away, and it remains to be seen if the New York Jets will trade off any of their pieces.

According to SNY's Connor Hughes , running back Breece Hall has been popular throughout the rumor mill.

Sources told Hughes, though, that the Jets haven't engaged in "realistic conversations" about dealing the 25-year-old. They say that the Jets like the idea of Hall and Braelon Allen as a 1-2 punch as a part of their future.

The Jets are 2-6 and won't be buying at the deadline, but if they view Hall as one of their pieces to become a contender beyond this season, it might take a lot for them to move him, even if teams across the league show interest.

Hughes reported it would take a second-round pick or a third-round pick and more to convince the Jets to seriously consider trading Hall.

Colts running back Jonathan Taylor has been the most speculated name on the trade block, so if a team loses on that sweepstakes, they might be willing to overpay for Hall. For now, though, it seems like the Jets are likely to keep their star rusher.

articles.title: New Jonathan Taylor Trade Rumors Reveal Giants' John Harbaugh's Stance to Land Colts RB
articles.summary: New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh is reportedly motivated to acquire Indianapolis Colts star running back Jonathan Taylor.
articles.body:
New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh is reportedly motivated to acquire Indianapolis Colts star running back Jonathan Taylor.

SNY's Connor Hughes reported that while some league sources "vary in whether they believe a Taylor trade actually gets done," several others are "hellbent in their conviction that Harbaugh will do whatever he can to get him, seeing an opportunity for New York to make a run."

In his first year in the Big Apple, Harbaugh has led the Giants to the top spot in the NFC East with a 4-2-1 record. However, New York's rushing attack has struggled to find consistency this year, and starter Cam Skattebo is hobbled by a hamstring injury.

Harbaugh knows how important it is to have a workhorse running back, as he spent his final few years with the Baltimore Ravens feeding carries to five-time Pro Bowler Derrick Henry. Taylor would undoubtedly be able to handle a similar workload, but Hughes noted that there's some skepticism about whether he gets traded by Tuesday.

"Others, familiar with what the Colts are asking for, believe the price is so steep Indianapolis isn't actually interested in dealing him," Hughes stated. "He'll remain with them throughout this season, with a trade revisited in March."

The Giants were expected to be rebuilding in their first year under Harbaugh, but he's instituted a swift turnaround that provides hope for a playoff run. With the right moves, New York could put itself in a position to compete against the elite teams in the NFC. It remains to be seen if Harbaugh will get his wish to acquire Taylor.

articles.title: Shedeur Sanders, Joe Milton Among 7 NFL Backup QBs Starting in Week 9 Amid QB1 Injuries
articles.summary: Backup quarterbacks — and even some third-stringers — have taken their fair share of regular season snaps throughout the first half of the 2026 NFL season. Several quarterback injuries are forcing teams across the league to turn to their backups once again in Week 9.
articles.body:
Backup quarterbacks — and even some third-stringers — have taken their fair share of regular season snaps throughout the first half of the 2026 NFL season. Several quarterback injuries are forcing teams across the league to turn to their backups once again in Week 9.

Seven teams will be starting backup quarterbacks, including five that will be starting their first game of the season.

The Baltimore Ravens are turning to undrafted rookie quarterback Joey Fagnano, who was serving as their emergency third-string option until starter Lamar Jackson and backup Tyler Huntley both suffered significant injuries in a nightmarish 36-10 loss against the Buffalo Bills in Week 8. Baltimore is finalizing a trade with the Arizona Cardinals for quarterback Jacoby Brissett, but the transaction won't be processed in time for their matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars on Thursday Night Football.

The Seattle Seahawks are expecting to start quarterback Drew Lock after starter Sam Darnold suffered a quad injury during Monday night's game against the Chicago Bears. Lock was forced into action earlier this season after Darnold suffered a glute injury in the season opener. He led Seattle to a 13-10 victory over the New England Patriots in Week 1 and defeated the Arizona Cardinals in a 31-7 blowout in Week 2.

Cleveland Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders is expected to make his season debut against the New Orleans Saints. Starting quarterback Deshaun Watson has led the Browns to an impressive 5-3 record, but he entered the NFL's concussion protocol after reporting concussion symptoms to the team on Tuesday.

Quarterback Joe Milton will make his first career start for the Philadelphia Eagles, who benched backup quarterback Tanner McKee following a 27-10 loss against the Washington Commanders. The Eagles have lost six consecutive games, including all three of McKee's starts.

Arizona Cardinals quarterback Gardner Minshew earned the starting role after he stepped in and led his team to an electric comeback against the Dallas Cowboys last Sunday. Although Brissett, who was benched during the game, was traded to Baltimore earlier this week, Minshew may not have a long leash with rookie quarterback Carson Beck waiting in the wings.

Quarterback J.J. McCarthy will make his second start for the New York Giants after leading them to a 27-21 overtime victory against the Houston Texans. The Giants acquired the third-year passer in a trade with the Minnesota Vikings after losing quarterback Jaxson Dart to a season-ending injury, and McCarthy replaced backup Jameis Winston, who was benched during a Week 6 loss.

The Minnesota Vikings will start quarterback Carson Wentz for a primetime matchup against the Buffalo Bills on Monday night after starter Kyler Murray was ruled out with a hamstring injury. Wentz previously stepped in to provide relief after Murray suffered a concussion in the team's regular-season opener. Although Wentz helped Minnesota pick up a pair of victories over their first two games, the credit for the team's success largely belongs to their top-ranked defense.

articles.title: Bill Belichick, snubbed from Pro Football Hall of Fame last year, among 5 coach nominees advancing in candidacy for 2027 class
articles.summary: Belichick's exclusion from the 2026 class drew ire throughout the football world.
articles.body:
The Pro Football Hall of Fame voting process came under fire and was thrust under a microscope last winter when Bill Belichick, arguably the greatest coach in NFL history, was denied first-ballot status .

Almost a year later, the Hall is moving forward in its annual consideration of potential new inductees. Belichick is once again up for enshrinement.

He's among five former NFL head coaches — the others being Tom Coughlin, Mike Holmgren, Dan Reeves and Mike Shanahan — who have advanced in their candidacy to be elected into the 2027 class, the Hall announced Thursday .

Members from the coach subcommittee whittled down a list that originally included 14 nominees. Next, the subcommittee will thoroughly review the five remaining coaches in contention on Nov. 17, when it meets virtually to pick one of them to present to the full selection committee.

Belichick, Coughlin, Holmgren, Reeves and Shanahan all reached this stage of the selection process last year. Ultimately, Belichick — best known for leading the New England Patriots to six Super Bowl victories during his dynastic run as the franchise's head coach — was picked as the candidate from that category to be up for election.

Keep in mind, of a class' 15 finalists presented at the selection committee's annual meeting, only one coach and one "contributor" are included. The other 13 nominees are modern-era players.

A coach hasn't been enshrined into the Hall since former Cardinals and Chargers frontman Don Coryell went in posthumously as part of the 2023 class.

To be enshrined, a candidate must receive at least 80% approval from the member selection committee. Previously, that usually meant a candidate needed 40 votes. Since, however, the board of selectors has shrunk to 28, and just 25 of them will actually vote .

Even though Belichick was the subcommittee's pick to be in the running for induction last year, he still had to meet that 80% threshold while competing with a contributor — ironically, Patriots owner Robert Kraft — and three "seniors" — Kenny Anderson, Roger Craig and L.C. Greenwood — in a separate part of the ballot. A minimum of one person and a maximum of three from those combined categories could be elected, per then-existing Hall bylaws.

Through all of that complicated mess, Belichick fell short of the necessary votes , leading to ubiquitous outrage, with countless people vouching for Belichick, including his longtime quarterback, Tom Brady, and even Kraft .

Craig wound up emerging from the group of nominees that featured Belichick last year . The iconic San Francisco 49ers running back eventually gave a touching pre-recorded speech upon his induction, during which he divulged that he has vascular dementia.

Back in September, significant changes were announced to the Hall's selection process. One of those was the elimination of the "seniors" category (every player will now be considered in the same pool).

Another was the reduction of the selection committee, effectively from 50 to 25 members (there are three alternates in the current system).

Under the Hall's latest bylaws, an induction class can consist of between three and seven honorees. It still takes 80% approval for enshrinement.

Also notable, the Hall decided its selection committee will return to discussing and submitting their final votes in person . That dialogue, in conjunction with the final voting process, had been held virtually since the COVID-19 pandemic, as reported by The Associated Press .

In early 2027, the selection committee will cast ballots to determine who earns spots in the upcoming class.

On Wednesday, the Hall announced that Kraft is one of the five contributors who have advanced in their candidacy to be elected into the 2027 class.

The class will be announced at "NFL Honors" in Los Angeles in February ahead of Super Bowl LXI, then enshrined in August in Canton, Ohio.

articles.title: Jets' Breece Hall Deactivated Twitter Account Due to Threats, Negative Comments Amid Injury
articles.summary: New York Jets running back Breece Hall had to quiet the noise after some fans took things too far.
articles.body:
New York Jets running back Breece Hall had to quiet the noise after some fans took things too far.

Hall told reporters on Thursday that he deactivated his X account because of negative comments and threats he received while he was sidelined with a quad injury for the last five weeks.

After opening the season with a 102-yard performance in a win over the Tennessee Titans, Hall combined for just 61 yards over the next two games. He was forced to exit New York's Week 3 loss to the Detroit Lions after injuring his quad, and he hasn't played since.

Jets head coach Aaron Glenn told reporters earlier this week that Hall is "trending in the right direction." He's been practicing on a limited basis for the past two weeks while the team takes a cautious approach with his recovery.

During Hall's absence, third-year running back Braelon Allen has emerged as a reliable ball-carrier, racking up 504 yards in his five games as the starter. It remains to be seen how New York will utilize both running backs when Hall returns.

The Jets (2-6) are facing a tough matchup on Sunday against the Kansas City Chiefs (5-2), so they could use as much help as they can get. Hall can silence his doubters if he returns to the lineup and helps the team end its three-game skid.

articles.title: Packers' Matt LaFleur Reacts to Jordan Love, Wife's Blind Ref Halloween Costumes in Viral Video
articles.summary: Green Bay Packers head coach Matt LaFleur was amused by quarterback Jordan Love and his wife dressing up as blind referees for Halloween.
articles.body:
Green Bay Packers head coach Matt LaFleur was amused by quarterback Jordan Love and his wife dressing up as blind referees for Halloween.

"I don't know how to answer this one, you didn't prepare me for this question," LaFleur told reporters Thursday. "He did send me the clip and I thought it was pretty hilarious. But I probably should refrain from giving my two cents on that."

On Oct. 25, the Packers suffered a 20-17 loss to the Detroit Lions in which the officiating was called out by players after the game.

Green Bay has been called for 71 penalties this season, the second-most in the NFL.

Still, the Packers are in the mix for the NFC North crown with a 5-3 record through eight games.

Love has put together a strong year, as he's thrown for a league-leading 2,246 yards while completing 61.5 percent of his passes. He's also tossed 16 touchdowns compared to six interceptions.

Green Bay is currently preparing for a matchup with the New England Patriots on Sunday. Kickoff is at 4:25 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Travis Kelce Reveals Perfect Holiday on Video, Chiefs TE's 1st Christmas Since Marrying Taylor Swift
articles.summary: A few months after marrying mega pop star Taylor Swift, Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce shared his "perfect holiday" in an advertisement with Tommy Hilfiger.
articles.body:
A few months after marrying mega pop star Taylor Swift, Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce shared his "perfect holiday" in an advertisement with Tommy Hilfiger.

The brand's winter campaign collaborated with Kelce, who described his first Christmas season married to Swift in the video. It was his second ad campaign with Tommy Hilfiger after doing a spot with them back in September.

The 37-year-old said he enjoys time with his family and a Christmas Day night game with the Chiefs.

"I'm excited for this year to be my first Christmas as a married man," Kelce says in the commercial. "Hi, I'm Travis Kelce and this is my perfect holiday: Have a night game on Christmas day and with my entire family."

He added that his mother baking blueberry muffins would be included in his perfect day:

The rest of the campaign includes New York Knicks guard Josh Hart and Liverpool players Florian Wirtz, Dominik Szoboszlai and Jérémy Jacquet.

Kelce and Swift spent Christmas together for the first time last year when they were engaged, with both of their families.

"I love all the old traditions and can't wait to start some new ones," he said in the video. "I start celebrating as that tree goes up."

articles.title: Caleb Williams celebrates Democrats winning midterms as concerns about him becoming the face of the NFL grow
articles.summary: Caleb Williams celebrated Democrats' projected House and Senate control, raising questions about a politically vocal NFL star's impact on the league.
articles.body: Bears quarterback Caleb Williams is enthused about the results of the 2026 midterms. Since Tuesday, he has posted several social media videos celebrating the Democrats’ projected control of the House and Senate. He specifically shared victory speeches from James Talarico (D, Texas) and Jon Ossoff (D, Georgia). The political views of an athlete are not inherently newsworthy. But Williams’ interest in social issues is more consequential than that of the typical player. BEARS PROVE THEY ARE NFC NORTH'S MOST COMPLETE TEAM WITH COMMANDING WIN OVER SEAHAWKS At just 24 years old, he is on pace to become the face of the NFL. The distinction matters. Patrick Mahomes has been the biggest star in the NFL since 2020, when he won his first of three Super Bowls. He is now 31 years old. He is coming off a torn ACL and has not been as dynamic in recent years. Josh Allen, whom general managers ranked the best quarterback in the sport, is around the same age as Mahomes. If one had to bet on a quarterback to win a Super Bowl over the next five years, the most obvious answer would be Caleb Williams. He has elevated himself to elite status this season. He has the premier head coach in Ben Johnson, who is just 40 years old. The Bears’ front office has assembled a top roster, most recently with the addition of All Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons. Williams leading Chicago to its first Super Bowl since 1986, combined with his flashy style of play, would propel him to megastar status. Face of the league, you might say. Williams would be a departure from the players who held that title before him. Mahomes, Tom Brady and Peyton Manning were mostly apolitical, putting the shield before their individual brands. Their personalities were rarely part of the discussion. In fact, Mahomes has repeatedly stated that he does not want to use his platform to discuss political or social causes. Quietly, the NFL is thrilled with that decision. Williams is different. He openly supports the Democratic Party. He previously deemed Jan. 6 an example of "#whiteprivilege." He participated in a BLM protest in support of George Floyd, who he said "could have been [me]." Williams recently generated headlines for wandering the sidelines in sunglasses during the United States national anthem, drawing comparisons to the demonstrations involving LeBron James and WNBA players. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Beyond his politics, Williams is less buttoned up in his presentation than the standard franchise quarterback. He frequently clashes with reporters during press conferences. Last month, he accused reporters of falsely reporting on his injury. He then refused to state what he believed the truth about the injury was. On Monday, Williams suggested he could become more influential in Chicago than Michael Jordan after the Bears’ win over the Seahawks. "When I was brought here, they told me that even through the times of Jordan and things like that, winning his championships, it's still a Chicago Bears town," Williams told ESPN. Aaron Rodgers is perhaps the best example of a star quarterback exhibiting such a personality. The difference is that Rodgers did not become a polarizing figure until later in his career, when he was more of a side character. Williams has the chance to be the main character in the NFL for the next decade. That creates a complicated dynamic for the league. The NFL is undoubtedly intrigued with Williams’ play and the possibility of him returning the Chicago Bears to prominence. Still, his persona is a concern. Political commentaries often turn shared cultural products into partisan battlegrounds. That is bad business. The numbers prove that. It took nearly a decade for the NFL to regain popularity among Republican viewers following the Colin Kaepernick kneeling controversy. The political discourse surrounding Bad Bunny contributed to record-setting viewership losses during last year’s Super Bowl halftime show. Bud Light’s partnership with Dylan Mulvaney, which celebrated his 365 Days of Girlhood, dropped its market cap by $27 billion in 2023. Williams supported a similar message by celebrating transgenderism on his painted fingernails last season. The NFL can bury wide receivers masquerading as activists on Instagram. Hiding the opinions of a star quarterback in Chicago is much harder. It is unreasonable to believe Williams’ persona and attitude will not become part of the story if he comes to represent the NFL brand. Recent trends in entertainment suggest that Caleb Williams is not the ideal avatar for the next era of the NFL. That is concerning because his play suggests he is the top candidate to become exactly that. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP For a counter perspective, Front Office Sports reporter Ryan Glasspiegel argues that Williams’ polarizing personality could benefit the league. "I don’t think it will hurt because, whether people love or hate him, at least he’s very interesting. If he wins big, which it seems he is on the trajectory to, and people tune in because they want to watch him lose, that’s ultimately good for the league, which is in the attention business," Glasspiegel told OutKick. The NFL better hope that is the case. Speaking of Michael Jordan comparisons, Republicans buy streaming services too.

articles.title: Ravens officially place Lamar Jackson, Tyler Huntley on IR with thumb, turf toe injuries
articles.summary: Baltimore also activated former UFL quarterback Austin Reed to the 53-man roster after signing him earlier this week.
articles.body:
The Baltimore Ravens will officially be without their top two quarterbacks for the near future: The team announced Thursday that it has placed both Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley on injured reserve .

The Ravens also activated UFL quarterback Austin Reed to the 53-man roster after signing him earlier this week . Reed will be the backup for undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano, who is set to make his first career start on Thursday against the Jacksonville Jaguars.

Jackson injured his thumb during Sunday's 36-10 loss to the Buffalo Bills on Baltimore's first offensive play. Jackson was making his return from a three-week absence with a high-ankle sprain, and he got injured on his first throw since Week 4 against the Tennessee Titans.

Bills linebacker Greg Rousseau made contact with Jackson's hand while attempting to defend the pass, and Jackson immediately walked off the field and into the Baltimore locker room.

The Ravens quickly ruled him out of the rest of the game with the thumb injury. Head coach Jesse Minter told reporters postgame that Jackson would require surgery on his injured thumb and a stint on injured reserve.

The Ravens did not reveal Sunday the precise nature of Jackson's injury, only that he had injured the thumb on his throwing hand. Asked at the time if the injury was season-ending, Minter said, "We'll see ."

Huntley, meanwhile, was diagnosed with a turf toe injury that is reportedly season-ending . Huntley, a career backup, started three games this season while Jackson was out with the ankle injury.

The injury is a critical blow for the Ravens and Jackson, whose recent seasons have been marred by injury. Jackson's a two-time MVP and one of the game's best players when healthy. When Jackson's available, the Ravens are regularly considered Super Bowl contenders.

Still, help is reportedly on the way, with Baltimore reportedly acquiring Jacoby Brissett in a trade with the Arizona Cardinals. The trade will reportedly not be completed until this weekend, meaning that Brissett cannot start for the Ravens on Thursday; he is reportedly expected to be the starter in Week 10.

How will injuries impact Jackson's contract talks?

Both leg and back injuries sidelined Jackson for four games in 2025 and limited his play in others. The result for the Ravens was a disappointing 8-9 campaign that fell short of the playoffs.

Jackson missed five regular games in each of the 2021 and 2022 seasons. Including Sunday's game in which he played just one snap, Jackson has missed a total of 21 games since his rookie campaign in 2018. The 4-4 Ravens now face another season of fighting for a playoff spot with their MVP quarterback on the sideline.

The injury arrives at a critical juncture in Jackson's career as he is on the fourth year of a five-year, $260 million contract. Team owner Steve Bisciotti has expressed his desire to make Jackson a Raven for life, but the two sides reportedly haven't engaged in substantial contract negotiations .

Now those contract talks and decisions will take place in the context of another of Jackson's seasons significantly limited by injury.

articles.title: Dak Prescott Reacts to George Pickens Trade Rumors Amid Cowboys Struggles Ahead of NFL Deadline
articles.summary: Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott weighed in on the trade buzz surrounding wide receiver George Pickens following a 3-5 start to the 2026 season.
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott weighed in on the trade buzz surrounding wide receiver George Pickens following a 3-5 start to the 2026 season.

"People say a lot of things I don't believe, so I'm not listening to that one, either," Prescott said Thursday, per Jon Machota of The Athletic. "George is a great teammate. And I say that in the sense of, he's gonna do whatever is asked, he's gonna do whatever is called. If it's to go block, if it's to just go run a guy off, he's gonna do that. He believes in just doing the right thing, and the ball will come his way at times. And so, that's not on George."

ESPN's Dan Graziano previously reported that opposing teams are "wondering" if Pickens could become available on the trade market if Dallas loses to the Indianapolis Colts in Week 9.

That doesn't necessarily mean the Cowboys are open to a deal, though.

NFL Network's Ian Rapoport also reported that "there's nothing here and that it is not happening" regarding Dallas possibly trading Pickens.

The receiver reportedly sought a long-term contract or a trade during the offseason, although he ultimately signed the franchise tag for one year and $27.3 million.

Pickens is now set to hit free agency in 2027, but the Cowboys can choose to tag him again. Both sides could agree to a long-term deal as well.

For now, Pickens is focusing on helping Dallas bounce back from its slow start to the season.

While he hasn't performed at the same level as his breakout 2025 campaign in which he racked up 1,429 receiving yards and earned his first Pro Bowl nod, he's remained productive this year.

In eight games, Pickens has hauled in 39 receptions for 533 yards and two touchdowns. Prescott owns a 106.1 passer rating when targeting Pickens, according to Pro Football Focus .

The 2026 NFL trade deadline is on Tuesday at 4 p.m. ET.

articles.title: 'S--t is Frustrating,' CeeDee Lamb Opens Up on Cowboys' Offensive Struggles Amid Losing Record
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys' defense held them back from reaching the playoffs last year despite an incredible offense, but that hasn't been the case this year.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys' defense held them back from reaching the playoffs last year despite an incredible offense, but that hasn't been the case this year.

While Dallas' defense has continued to struggle, the offense has likewise had a rough year. Star wide receiver CeeDee Lamb is clearly upset with how things have gone for his unit.

"We stop ourselves. That s--t is frustrating. It's annoying. I hate it," Lamb told reporters Thursday. "Then ultimately we end up losing, so there's that."

Last season, the Cowboys had a top-five offense but missed the playoffs because of a defense that ranked among the bottom of the league. This season, Dallas' offense ranks 13th in yards per game (342) and seventh in points per game (27.4).

While their scoring numbers on the surface don't look too bad, it hasn't been enough to make up for the Cowboys' defense, which ranks last in yards allowed per game (385.4) and sixth in points allowed per game (26.6).

Dallas could still reach the playoffs, but it will need its offense to return to what it was last year to try to answer for the defensive woes.

articles.title: Travis Kelce throws Patrick Mahomes under the bus with blunt admission about Chiefs' controversial loss
articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs are still dealing with the fallout from their painful Week 8 defeat to the Denver Broncos, and the latest comments from Travis
articles.body: The Kansas City Chiefs are still dealing with the fallout from their painful Week 8 defeat to the Denver Broncos, and the latest comments from Travis Kelce have added another twist to the conversation. While Patrick Mahomes and Andy Reid questioned a crucial penalty that hurt Kansas City's chances of winning, Kelce has taken a different position. The veteran tight end backed the officials' decision, admitting that the Chiefs committed a penalty. His comments also come as Mahomes addresses another major talking point surrounding the team's late-game decisions and Reid's reluctance to use quarterback sneaks.Travis Kelce disagrees with Patrick Mahomes over Chiefs' controversial penaltyThe Chiefs had a golden opportunity to steal a victory against Denver after reaching the goal line in the closing seconds. However, a false start penalty pushed Kansas City into a difficult position before the offense failed to convert on fourth down.The call quickly became a major talking point, particularly after Mahomes suggested that officials might have allowed the play to continue in a high-pressure situation.Speaking on Wednesday's episode of the New Heights podcast, Travis discussed the decision alongside his brother, Jason Kelce. Unlike his quarterback, the Chiefs tight end had little doubt about whether the officials made the right call.“A lot of people are saying this wasn’t a penalty; I’m going to go on record and say that this is definitely a penalty,” Jason said.Travis agreed with his brother's assessment, acknowledging the movement that led to the flag.“Yeah, he flinches,” the Chiefs tight end admitted.However, Kelce refused to make the penalty the sole reason behind Kansas City's defeat. He believed the offense still had an opportunity to finish the drive.“At the end of the day, we still had another play,” Travis said. “I’ll take my guy Pat Mahomes on the six-yard line with the game on the line; I’ll take that any day of the week. So we gotta execute at the end even more. We can’t let the penalty absolutely deflate us and not let us execute at the end of the game.”Patrick Mahomes addresses Andy Reid's quarterback sneak decisionMeanwhile, Mahomes has another issue to address following the Chiefs' 28-24 loss. Kansas City entered the fourth quarter with an 11-point advantage but failed to protect its lead.One particular decision drew criticism. On third-and-goal from the Denver one-yard line, Reid called a handoff to Kenneth Walker III instead of attempting a quarterback sneak. Walker was stopped short, wasting a valuable scoring opportunity.Mahomes made it clear that he would not hesitate to take the ball himself if the situation demanded it.“I’m going to do whatever it takes to win,” Mahomes said. “Quarterback sneak, whatever it is, it’s not like I’m scared to put my body on the line. That’s how I’ve played. It’s gotten me in trouble sometimes, and sometimes it’s helped the team. That’s stuff we’ll continue to evaluate and work on to make ourselves better for future references.”The quarterback also acknowledged that such a decision must deliver results.“If I do that, it better work,” Mahomes said. “I understand people watch the film and see stuff and want you to go out there and make it happen. But, the play call is what we call, and we want to execute that play. That’s stuff that we evaluate and learn from. We’ll try to be better the next few weeks. If I call my own number, it’s got to work.”With Kansas City facing questions about its execution, play-calling and late-game composure, the pressure is growing on Reid and Mahomes to find answers before their next challenge.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Mike McDaniel Making Chargers' Play-Calling Change Amid Offensive Struggles, NFL-Worst Record
articles.summary: Los Angeles Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel is heading upstairs after an 0-7 start to the season.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel is heading upstairs after an 0-7 start to the season.

McDaniel told reporters Thursday he has spoken with head coach Jim Harbaugh about calling plays from the coaches' box ahead of Sunday's matchup against the visiting Houston Texans.

"I won't be in the same spot... I'm being very open-minded with all things," McDaniel said.

Hot Seat Check on Struggling NFL Coordinators 🌡️

Harbaugh confirmed McDaniel would continue calling plays after the Chargers continued their winless season with a 24-9 loss to the Los Angeles Rams last Sunday.

"It seems like a good action to take based on how things have gone this year, and realistically something I've only brought up because I'm very confident in the rest of the offensive coaching staff and how they're able to set the tone and communicate information on the sidelines," McDaniel said.

He added the "impetus" for making the change was his experience working with San Francisco 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan, who called plays from the box when serving as offensive coordinator for the Atlanta Falcons in 2015 and 2016.

McDaniel also said when discussing the decision he felt he should take on some of the "burden" being carried by Justin Herbert after the quarterback threw an NFL-high 10 interceptions during his team's winless start.

"To their credit, the guys see a vision of how they can play to the standard with which we have yet to meet... I have reasonable expectation for things to improve," McDaniel said.

The Chargers are heading into the weekend ranked 26th in the NFL in total passing yards and 18th in total rushing yards.

Harbaugh said after his team put up 295 total yards of offense but scored no touchdowns and committed two turnovers against the Rams he would be sticking with both Herbert and McDaniel going forward.

When asked after Sunday's loss what gave him confidence to stick with his offensive coordinator, Harbaugh said it would be "team effort" to improve going forward.

The Chargers are preparing to face a Texans defense that has allowed the fifth-most passing yards against in the NFL so far this season. McDaniel will hope his bird's-eye view can help Herbert take advantage of those struggles when Sunday's matchup kicks off Sunday at 4:05 p.m. ET at SoFi Stadium.

articles.title: CJGJ Release Explained by Bills' Joe Brady, How Spitting Incident Impacted Decision
articles.summary: Buffalo Bills head coach Joe Brady detailed the team's recent decision to release safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson.
articles.body:
Buffalo Bills head coach Joe Brady detailed the team's recent decision to release safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson.

"There was a lot to evaluate," Brady told reporters Thursday, via Mike Florio of Pro Football Talk. "You know, we got together and figured out, 'Hey, this is what we felt like this was the best thing to do for the Buffalo Bills.' I have so much love for [C.J.]. Like, I really do. I loved getting to coach him. I loved being around him. I loved — I did love the edge, and his personality allowing him to be him, right?, and as a person. So that didn't make the decision easy at all.

"But we also have to be an organization that, you know, it's unfortunate obviously what happened, you know? But it also opened a door and an opportunity for guys the other day, and that was a part of evaluation. And seeing how those guys kind of played, and you know with a lot of the roster moves. And, again, this wasn't — we didn't come out of the game post Vegas and say, 'This is what we were going to do. We're just gonna do this the following Monday.' We were, you know, the plan was him being here and we were going to evaluate it after the game in Baltimore. And we felt like with some of the moving parts we had to do it was the best interests of the football team."

Gardner-Johnson was released by the Bills on Tuesday after serving a one-game suspension that he received from the NFL for spitting towards Las Vegas Raiders tight end Brock Bowers during a Week 6 matchup between the two teams.

The safety later apologized for his actions on social media.

"My passion and competitive nature have always been a huge part of who I am, but I also understand that there is a line that should never be crossed," Gardner-Johnson wrote in a post on his Instagram story (h/t CBS Sports' Zachary Pereles ). "The gesture I made toward my opponent was inappropriate, unnecessary, and not a reflection of the respect I have for him or this game. There is no excuse for my actions, and I take full accountability. No matter how emotional or intense the competition gets, I have to hold myself to a higher standard."

The 28-year-old has faced punishment from the NFL on several occasions throughout his career, as he's racked up 15 fines across his eight seasons in the league (via Spotrac ).

Gardner-Johnson was in the midst of his inaugural campaign in Buffalo after joining the team on a one-year contract worth up to $6 million in free agency.

He started in each of the Bills' first six games of the season, recording 26 tackles, two passes defended and one interception. Gardner-Johnson was part of a struggling Buffalo secondary, as it currently owns the NFL's No. 30 pass defense by allowing 254.7 yards per game through the air.

After suiting up for five teams over the past four seasons, the veteran is now searching for a new landing spot before the end of the year.

articles.title: 'Wipe those tears from our eyes and play like 46': Lions defense turns Jack Campbell tragedy into fuel
articles.summary: Kelvin Sheppard reveals the emotional fourth-down blitz call he made for Jack Campbell and how "play like 46" became the Detroit Lions' rallying cry.
articles.body: The pain of watching Jack Campbell collapse helplessly on the Ford Field turf Sunday has not completely subsided for the Detroit Lions. It certainly is not forgotten by teammates on defense that spent those horrible moments wiping away tears as their captain lay motionless with a neck injury. But four days later, following Campbell's mostly positive report about having lower body motion, the focus has shifted to how to continue handling the situation. The prayers persist. That hasn't stopped. LIONS' JACK CAMPBELL OPENS UP ABOUT NECK INJURY, ANNOUNCES LOWER BODY MOVEMENT BUT ACKNOWLEDGES CHALLENGES But the anguish, despair and despondency are yielding to something different. Something better: Inspiration. "You're kidding yourself to say it's not hard for the players to see something like that happen to anyone, let alone a player of his stature, of his makeup, of his heart," Lions defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard said on Thursday. "And to think these players are going to walk back in here like nothing happened? "So the theme has been, let's prepare and play like 46 – every day." Sheppard said a key fourth-down calls he made toward the end of Sunday's game was calling a blitz against the Minnesota Vikings when that is not typical for the Lions. He said the message to players then was, "we're about to do this for 46," which is Campbell's number. That approach has extended through this week. "I wake up [thinking] 'what would 46 want me to do today?' Sheppard said. "Would he want us to sulk and feel sorry? I can guarantee you, y'all know Jack, absolutely not. He'd be p---ed off if he found out guys were crying and guys were about him. That's just his makeup. "So that's what we're doing in everything we do. Every meeting I told the unit, every walkthrough, every play, you all know how Jack prepares. You all know how he plays. The way you honor him is to wipe those tears from your eyes and make sure we prepare and play like him. "So that's the thing moving forward to this week." This is good coaching. Sheppard cannot deny the emotions his players invested on the scary and uncertain moments while Campbell was being placed on a immobilization board and carted off the field. But the NFL season has not stopped since the game moved ahead. And like the game, the season continues for the Lions. And so Sheppard is asking his defensive players to accept something horrible, acknowledge it, and not only overcome it but turn it into a tool. "That is," Sheppard repeated "the theme for the week." articles.title: First, 'meatball sub,' and now 'deli meat.' Even Justin Herbert's passes are getting the Subway treatment
articles.summary: Justin Herbert said he was unaware of comments by Rams safety Quentin Lake, who said on a podcast that the Chargers quarterback was "throwing deli meat" duri...
articles.body:
Justin Herbert famously loves Subway subs. During his rookie season in 2020, the Chargers quarterback told GQ magazine he was "living off" the sandwiches, consuming both a Steak Philly sub and a Chicken & Bacon Ranch sub each night for dinner. He has since appeared in at least eight TV commercials for the restaurant franchise.

But the Chargers quarterback was making his own sandwiches Sunday — or at least that's how it seemed to an opposing defender who picked off one of his passes that afternoon.

"He was throwing deli meat out there," Rams safety Quentin Lake said this week on the "St. Brown Podcast," apparently joining the current inclination of using sandwich-related metaphors to describe bad passes.

"Was he?" asked Detroit Lions receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown , who co-hosts the podcast with his brother, former NFL receiver Equanimeous St. Brown .

"Bro, he's seeing ghosts," Lake told his former Mater Dei teammate as all three men started laughing.

"I don't know what's going on, but like we knew we were going to get a couple [interceptions], at least one," Lake added.

The Rams snagged two during their 24-9 victory over the Chargers. Midway through the first quarter, Lake stepped in front of a pass intended for Charlie Kolar and returned it 45 yards to the Chargers' 19-yard line, setting up a Rams field goal for a 3-0 lead.

Late in the third quarter, Rams cornerback Trent McDuffie also got a pick in front of Kolar and returned it 26 yards to the Chargers' 22-yard line. Two plays later, quarterback Matthew Stafford connected with receiver Puka Nacua for an 18-yard touchdown and a 24-9 lead.

Herbert completed 24 of 32 passes for 257 yards with no touchdowns. His struggles under new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniels are seen as a large factor in the Chargers' unexpected 0-7 record.

The seventh-year quarterback has thrown for five touchdowns and a league-high 10 interceptions this year, with at least one pick in each of this season's seven games. In 2024, Herbert finished the 17-game season with 23 touchdowns and only three interceptions.

This week wasn't the first time this season Herbert's passes have been described like a lunchtime menu item.

On Sept. 27, after Herbert threw a floater to then-Buffalo Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson, former NFL quarterback and current Fox broadcaster Tom Brady offered this on-air analysis: "Poor awareness. Poor decision. Throws him a meatball sub."

This season, random social media users have given other quarterbacks the Subway treatment, including New England's Drake Maye, Denver's Bo Nix, Cleveland's Deshawn Watson and even Kansas City's Patrick Mahomes, a two-time league MVP and three-time Super Bowl champion.

Herbert told reporters on Wednesday that he hadn't "heard anything about" Lake's comments.

"We're really just focused on what's going on in this building and playing football and doing what we can and doing our best to go put our best effort out on Sunday," Herbert said. "That's all that really matters. Anything outside of that is out of our control."

Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh didn't agree with Lake's assessment of Herbert's performance on Sunday.

"I don't see that," Harbaugh said. "Everybody's entitled to their opinion, [but] it's not what I see."

He added that he thought Herbert "did his job exceptionally well" against the Rams, except for "two throws he would have liked to have back."

This story originally appeared in Los Angeles Times .

Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver Rashee Rice has filed for bankruptcy in Texas, citing civil lawsuit settlements stemming from a 2024 car crash among his $3.45 million in debts.

The court filing submitted on Wednesday in the US Bankruptcy Court for the Northern District of Texas lists $677,054 in total personal property assets.

That includes Rice's Super Bowl ring from the Chiefs' victory over the San Francisco 49ers in the NFL's title game in February 2024, which according to the documents Rice used as collateral with Thomas McMurray, the lawyer representing him in pending civil litigations.

Rice was suspended for the first six games of the 2025 NFL season over his involvement in the 2024 high-speed crash in which his Lamborghini SUV was clocked at 119 mph (191.51 km/h) on a Dallas highway.

An ensuing multi-car crash left several injured and Rice fled on foot.

He apologized in a statement before turning himself in to authorities. Rice pleaded guilty to felony charges in the crash and was sentenced to five years of probation and 30 days' jail time.

The court documents filed Wednesday show Rice has been paying crash victim Kathryn Kuykendall through garnishment of his Chiefs paychecks, with $979,837 still owed.

The documents list as "disputed" a claim of $200,000 to former girlfriend Dacoda Jones, who in February accused him of assaulting her and launched a civil suit against him.

Three other claims amounting to $650,000 to three other crash victims are listed as "disputed".

Other debts include unsecured bank loans.

The 26-year-old Rice is in the final year of his rookie contract and is expected to make $1,560,711 in base salary in 2026.

Rice, who returned to action on Sunday after missing two games with a hamstring injury, has played in five games this season with 20 catches and two touchdowns.

articles.title: NFL trade deadline: 3 teams that could deal for Saints DB Justin Reid
articles.summary: Justin Reid could be on the move at the NFL trade deadline. AFC playoff teams like the Buffalo Bills and Jacksonville Jaguars could use his help.
articles.body:
Which New Orleans Saints players could be on the move at the Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline? The latest reporting has highlighted names like right guard Cesar Ruiz, linebacker Pete Werner, and running back Kendre Miller, but another one to watch is veteran safety Justin Reid . With no guarantees left on his contract in 2027 and a dearth of quality safety play around the league, he could have some appeal to teams in the playoff hunt. Reid doesn't generate many turnovers but he's a reliable tackler with meaningful postseason experience.

Sure, trading Reid wouldn't help the Saints' salary cap situation (saving about $650,000 this year and nearly breaking even in 2027). But trading the 29-year old would open up snaps for younger players with something to prove like Jordan Howden, who will be a free agent in the spring. Special teams aces Lorenzo Styles Jr. and Mike Reid could also compete for more snaps. It's important the Saints find out what they have in these guys on the bottom of the depth chart and determine if any of them can handle a larger role, or at least be part of the plan moving forwards. If the Saints can get another at-bat in the 2027 NFL Draft or improve the picks they already have, even better.

With that in mind, here are three trade proposals we'd hear out before next week's deadline.

New Orleans gets: 2027 sixth-round pick (No. 185)

Buffalo could use another safety after cutting former Saints draft pick C.J. Gardner-Johnson, who ranked third on the team in snaps played (394) and first missed tackles (9). Cole Bishop is an every-down starter at the other safety spot, but the Bills lack a proven commodity next to him. Damar Hamlin is a good backup but he only has two years of starting experience. Reid is someone Buffalo could lean on.

Jacksonville gets: S Justin Reid, 2028 seventh-round pick (TBD)

New Orleans gets: 2027 fifth-round pick (No. 164)

Antonio Johnson has played really well when healthy ( so much so that we targeted him in our bye week 2027 mock offseason ), and he's set to return from an ankle injury on Thursday Night Football . But the Jaguars have struggled to get consistency out of the other safety spot between Eric Murray and Rayuan Lane III. A steady veteran like Reid could be just what they need to lock things down on the back end.

Los Angeles gets: S Justin Reid, 2027 fifth- and sixth-round picks (Nos. 144 and 181)

New Orleans gets: 2027 fourth- and fifth-round picks (Nos. 128 and 163)

This deal is based off the Sydney Brown trade between the Philadelphia Eagles and Atlanta Falcons; New Orleans gets two better picks while offloading Reid's contract. Quentin Lake is holding it down in the box but Kamren Curl has struggled at free safety, and neither Kamren Kinchens nor Jaylen McCollough have held up well in coverage. The Rams are treading water at 4-4, and getting an upgrade without losing any picks (even if they're going to be picking later) has to be appealing after their big moves thus far.

articles.title: As Chargers' offense struggles, Mike McDaniel will move from the sideline to the booth
articles.summary: Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel will get a different perspective on his struggling offense on Sunday against the Texans.
articles.body:
Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel will get a different perspective on his struggling offense on Sunday against the Texans.

McDaniel said today that he will move upstairs to the booth to call plays after previously working from the sideline.

"One of the things that I want to try is call plays from the box to see adjustments for myself and communicate with the position coaches appropriately what things we can focus on between series," McDaniel said. "I won't be in the same spot."

Although the Chargers' offense has been among the worst in the NFL this season and head coach Jim Harbaugh has faced questions about whether he should fire his offensive coordinator, McDaniel insisted that he's not concerned about the criticism.

"My problem solving doesn't come from insecurity," McDaniel said. "I'm not trying to prove or justify anything."

The Chargers rank dead last in the NFL in scoring, having scored only 99 points this season, and they have an NFL-high 17 turnovers. McDaniel said he thinks it's worth trying something different while delegating some of what he had been doing on the sideline to the assistant coaches.

"Seems like a good action to take based on how things have gone this year, and realistically something that I've only brought up because I've observed, I'm very confident in the rest of the offensive coaching staff and how they're able to set the tone and communicate information on the sidelines. So I feel a little more comfortable to try that," McDaniel said.

If that doesn't work, Harbaugh's next step might be to move McDaniel from the booth to the unemployment line.

articles.title: Browns’ Harold Fannin Jr. lands on injury report ahead of Saints matchup
articles.summary: The Cleveland Browns have some injuries to deal with as the 2026 NFL season reaches its ninth week of action. Among the notable players on the team’s injury...
articles.body:
The Cleveland Browns have some injuries to deal with as the 2026 NFL season reaches its ninth week of action. Among the notable players on the team's injury report ahead of its Week 9 showdown against the New Orleans Saints at Caesars Superdome in New Orleans is tight end Harold Fannin Jr.

The second-year pro has been arguably the most important weapon downfield for Cleveland this season , but the team is facing the possibility of missing Fannin for the game in the Big Easy.

The Bowling Green Falcons product popped up on the Browns' injury report on Thursday with a lower-body issue, though he was able to practice in limited fashion with the team.

"Browns TE Harold Fannin Jr. was added to the injury report and limited with a groin injury. A groin injury prematurely ended his rookie season and kept him sidelined for much of the offseason workout program," Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN shared via a social media post on X, formerly Twitter.

Hopefully, this is nothing but a bit of maintenance on the part of the Browns, but it is still a reasonable cause for concern that Fannin is on the injury report this close to the matchup versus Tyler Shough and the Saints on the road.

Fannin still has a chance to practice in full and remove any doubts about his status for Sunday's game, so his situation is worth monitoring, especially given his importance to the Browns' attack.

A third-round pick by the Browns in the 2025 NFL Draft, Fannin is leading the team so far this season with 411 receiving yards to go along with three touchdowns on 35 receptions and 51 targets through eight games.
